## P191  approved source clauses -> controlled syntax tree -> typed rule records

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U01, U03, U17
reuses: P1 candidate extraction and source checking; P95 strict field contracts
new capability: Lark controlled-language compiler with explicit semantic acceptance
public basis: S01 clauses supply membership and approval examples. The controlled expressions are assessment-authored mappings, not publisher-supplied executable rules.

```
source snapshot + approved clause-to-rule mappings
-> preserve source selectors and character offsets (hashlib.sha256; unicodedata.normalize; declared offset-map adapter)
-> generate candidates only (ufal.udpipe.Pipeline.process; existing P1 adapter)
-> parse the approved controlled language (lark.Lark.parse; lark.Transformer.transform)
-> validate modality, negation scope, condition AST, exceptions, and authority fields (pydantic.BaseModel.model_validate)
-> bind derivations to source entities (rdflib.Graph.add; PROV-O predicates)
-> typed rule register + rejected or unresolved clauses
```

contract: Grammar and semantics are versioned separately. require, permit, and forbid are distinct. Boolean connectors have declared precedence. Source-candidate extraction cannot silently approve a mapping.

theoretical positive test: For the S01 four-voting-member minimum, an approved count >= 4 expression retains actor, integer threshold, and clause reference. The four-member boundary satisfies the expression; three does not.

theoretical adverse test: Treating the phrase "not merely" as an unconditional prohibition changes the meaning. The compiler must reject that unsupported construction or require an explicit approved mapping. Removing an exception or swapping actor/object also fails semantic acceptance.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. A grammar, typed AST, and source map can support deterministic compilation of a bounded controlled language. Unrestricted procedure-to-rule equivalence remains unestablished.

public-data limit: S01 tests a narrow governance domain. It supplies neither banking applicability nor a labeled corpus proving extraction accuracy.

required implementation and evidence: Implement the grammar and source-offset adapter; archive positive and counterexample mappings; run parse/print/parse, semantic mutation, and reviewer-acceptance tests. Report unsupported-clause coverage.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: rule-records.jsonl; controlled-language.ebnf; unresolved-clauses.json; semantic-test-results.json

Libraries and primary references: S01; L01; L06

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P192  typed request dimensions + rule scopes -> applicability evaluation -> scoped requirement candidates

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U02, U03
reuses: P4 policies; P6 typed records; P191 rule AST
new capability: Explicit scope algebra compiled through the new AST rather than action-lemma matching
public basis: S01 distinguishes voting and regular members. S03 selects controls from catalogs. Region, product, legal-entity, and channel values used in tests are declared analogues.

```
P191 rule records + request-dimension schema + typed request
-> validate enumerations and absent dimensions (pydantic.TypeAdapter.validate_python)
-> expand only finite declared domains (itertools.product; explicit scope adapter)
-> derive applicability and unresolved facts (clingo.Control.add/ground/solve)
-> check candidate consistency under the same scope encoding (z3.Solver.check)
-> preserve included, excluded, and unresolved reasons (pandas.DataFrame.merge with cardinality validation)
-> requirement candidates + applicability explanation rows
```

contract: Unknown and wildcard are different. A missing region never means all regions. A request may bind a set only where the dimension contract explicitly permits sets.

theoretical positive test: A voting-member rule applies to a voting-member request; the same rule is out of scope for a fully typed regular-member request. A missing member type stays unresolved.

theoretical adverse test: A fabricated catch-all converts missing member type into permission. A rejected enum, absent booking entity, or inconsistent multi-value binding blocks a definitive requirement manifest.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. Finite scope matching is expressible in existing rule and constraint engines once the cross-engine scope semantics are fixed.

public-data limit: Public control-profile selection is an analogue. Actual jurisdiction and legal-entity requirement tables are absent.

required implementation and evidence: Define scope set operations and three-way applicability; exhaustively enumerate the bounded test domain; keep grounded rule IDs for every candidate; independently evaluate a small truth table.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: applicable-requirements.json; excluded-rules.json; unresolved-dimensions.json

Libraries and primary references: S01; S03; L01; L03; L04

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P193  scoped obligations and prohibitions -> satisfiable overlap search -> contradiction register

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U03, U04
reuses: P2 solver checks; P192 scoped requirements
new capability: Conflict witnesses tied to overlapping scope and modality
public basis: S01 source-approved rules provide the base. Contradictory permit/forbid variants are explicitly injected test mutations.

```
P192 requirements + approved precedence policy
-> group by actor, action, object, and relevant effect identity (pandas.DataFrame.groupby)
-> encode scope intersections and contrary requirements (z3.And/Not/Implies)
-> track each source-backed assertion (z3.Solver.assert_and_track)
-> solve and extract conflict witnesses or tracked cores (Solver.check; Solver.model; Solver.unsat_core)
-> link findings to rule and source nodes (networkx.MultiDiGraph.add_edge; rdflib.Graph.add)
-> contradiction register + separate ambiguity and solver-undecided rows
```

contract: Different jurisdictions alone do not conflict. A permission is not automatically a requirement; conflict semantics and precedence must be declared. An unsat core is not claimed minimal without an explicit minimization test.

theoretical positive test: Injected require(action) and forbid(action) with an identical satisfiable scope produce a witnessed contradiction. Disjoint fully known scopes produce no same-scope contradiction.

theoretical adverse test: Globally conjoining all rules erases their scopes and yields false conflicts. Solver unknown or timeout must remain undecided. A missing authority cannot be repaired by an automatic deny-overrides assumption.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. The method detects contradictions in the encoded theory. It does not choose the legally correct rule.

public-data limit: Public clauses do not supply a precedence hierarchy for banking regulations or competing policy owners.

required implementation and evidence: Implement conflict semantics; assert a known overlap and a disjoint control case; test the witness independently; preserve solver settings and source IDs. Route owner resolution as new versioned input.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: conflict-witnesses.json; tracked-cores.json; unresolved-priorities.json

Libraries and primary references: S01; L04; L06

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P194  rule and control graph -> shape and completeness validation -> source-linked defect report

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U01, U04, U05, U17
reuses: P37 RDF graph; P95 schema contracts; P191 rule records
new capability: pySHACL validation over a declared complete target inventory
public basis: S03 control IDs, parameters, imports, and catalog structure. Mandatory internal owner and authority fields are assessment-defined additions.

```
P191 rule graph + expected control inventory + SHACL shapes
-> load local RDF and preserve stable identifiers (rdflib.Graph.parse)
-> validate required links and types (pyshacl.validate)
-> inspect results and focus-node references (rdflib.Graph.query)
-> compare validated target IDs with the independent expected inventory (set difference; pandas.merge)
-> link every defect to its source and failed shape (PROV-O links; Jinja2.Environment with StrictUndefined)
-> defect register + coverage report
```

contract: SHACL validates declared shapes, not truth. Zero targeted nodes cannot count as success when controls were expected. Missing owners remain missing.

theoretical positive test: A control with one valid source, one declared authority reference, and required evidence links conforms to the test shapes. Every expected control appears in the coverage reconciliation.

theoretical adverse test: Remove its actor link, mistype an evidence date, or remove the class that selects the node. The first two yield violations; the third must be caught by the independent target-inventory check.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. Shape validation plus target coverage supports graph integrity and prevents vacuous conformance.

public-data limit: OSCAL gives structural examples. It does not identify the authorized people for the target program.

required implementation and evidence: Implement shapes and explicit target inventory; run missing-property, duplicate-ID, wrong-datatype, and empty-target mutations; archive the full validation report.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: control-shapes.ttl; shacl-report.ttl; graph-defects.json; target-coverage.json

Libraries and primary references: S03; L02; L06

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P195  source revisions and text normalization -> stable span mapping -> semantic-change candidates

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U01, U17
reuses: P1 canonical text and byte checks; P120 content comparison
new capability: Lark-assisted token classification with bidirectional source-span mapping
public basis: S01 original prose and S02 optional values. Unicode, whitespace, and changed-negation cases are named mutations of these examples.

```
original text + revised text + normalization policy
-> hash each original byte sequence before decoding (hashlib.sha256; explicit codec)
-> preserve raw and normalized offsets (unicodedata.normalize; versioned span-map adapter)
-> tokenize supported controlled expressions (lark.Lark.lex)
-> compare original clauses and AST fields separately (difflib.SequenceMatcher.get_opcodes; typed AST comparison)
-> record derivation and version relationships (rdflib.Graph.add; PROV-O revision links)
-> source-change map + semantic-review candidates
```

contract: Offsets are tagged as bytes or Unicode code points. Normalization is not assumed length preserving. A cosmetic text change and a semantic change are different findings.

theoretical positive test: A whitespace-only change preserves the typed rule while updating its source hash and span map. A threshold edit from four to five changes the numeric AST field.

theoretical adverse test: A removed negation, altered exception, or combined Unicode character must not be hidden by normalized text equality. A pointer into the wrong source version is rejected.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. Exact text and AST comparison can identify changes within the supported representation. It cannot decide meaning for an unsupported paraphrase.

public-data limit: No public multilingual gold-standard policy corpus was ingested. Translation equivalence remains untested.

required implementation and evidence: Implement code-point/byte maps; require reverse span checks; exercise Unicode composition, insertion, and deletion; retain raw source versions.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: span-map.json; source-diff.json; semantic-review-queue.json

Libraries and primary references: S01; S02; L01; L06

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.

## P197  one approved decision AST -> independent engine adapters -> bounded decision equivalence

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U02, U03, U18
reuses: P54 input enumeration; P55 cross-engine checks; P191-P193
new capability: Hypothesis-generated semantic differential testing across the expanded rule representation
public basis: S01 membership minimum and approval-condition examples form a bounded oracle. They are not election outcomes.

```
approved AST + bounded domain + independent truth-table oracle
-> compile separate engine representations (Jinja2 render to Zen JDM; clingo.Control.add; z3 expressions)
-> generate boundaries, missing values, and contrary evidence (hypothesis.given; strategies; explicit adversarial fixtures)
-> evaluate each supported engine (zen.ZenDecision.evaluate; clingo.Control.solve; z3.Solver.check)
-> normalize result dimensions without losing unknown states (pydantic typed result adapter)
-> compare every result and source explanation with the oracle (pytest assertions; pandas comparison)
-> equivalence report + minimal failing examples
```

contract: Compare only a declared common semantic subset. Rule hit policy, default negation, missing values, and multiple answer sets need explicit mappings. Engines may refuse unsupported cases.

theoretical positive test: For fully known integer counts within the test domain, the count >= 4 rule agrees with an independent arithmetic table at 3, 4, and 5 and throughout enumeration.

theoretical adverse test: A missing count cannot become zero in one engine and unknown in another. A multiple-answer-set case must not be treated as a unique decision. Common compiler errors are tested against the independent oracle.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. Differential testing can expose adapter disagreement and oracle mismatch. Agreement on examples is not proof of arbitrary-language equivalence.

public-data limit: Public examples cover simple policies. Complex domain exceptions and deployed engine-version compatibility remain untested.

required implementation and evidence: Implement three adapters; freeze engine versions after tests; preserve failing examples; record supported features and exhaustive versus sampled coverage.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: engine-equivalence.json; counterexamples.json; supported-semantics.json

Libraries and primary references: S01; L03; L04; L05; L07

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P198  scoped decision rows -> gaps and overlaps -> totality qualification

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U02, U03
reuses: P54 enumeration; P192 applicability; P197 adapters
new capability: Solver-backed coverage obligations and generated missing-value cases
public basis: S01 provides a public numeric boundary; S03 provides include/exclude examples. Combined rules are assessment-authored test tables.

```
decision rows + closed request domain + explicit unknown-state policy
-> validate row predicates and output types (P191 Lark AST; pydantic)
-> enumerate small domains (itertools.product)
-> seek uncovered and conflicting inputs symbolically (z3.Solver.check; model extraction)
-> generate threshold-neighbor mutations (Hypothesis strategies)
-> compare row hits under the selected policy (zen.ZenDecision.evaluate with trace)
-> gap/overlap witnesses + qualified coverage statement
```

contract: Totality is relative to the declared domain. An unknown dimension has its own route. Multiple rows may coexist under a collect policy; contradictory outputs still require resolution.

theoretical positive test: Rows n < 4 and n >= 4 partition the declared nonnegative integer domain. An explicit missing-n route covers incomplete input separately.

theoretical adverse test: Changing the second row to n > 4 exposes the gap at n = 4. Adding an incompatible n >= 3 row exposes overlap; unsupported enum values remain outside the certified domain.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT. Finite enumeration or a decidable solver encoding supports a precise coverage claim, with counterexamples when it fails.

public-data limit: A table can be complete over a wrong domain. Owner acceptance of request dimensions remains required.

required implementation and evidence: Archive domain schema and row policy; run the boundary gap mutation and conflicting-output mutation; retain solver undecided states and sampled-coverage labels.

## P201  records without shared IDs -> probabilistic linkage -> reviewed identity candidates

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U07, U08, U17
reuses: P6 typed records; P154 ambiguity-preserving reconciliation; P199 gates
new capability: Splink record linkage with an explicit abstention and review band
public basis: S07 provides labeled simulated duplicate records. Names, addresses, and errors are simulation data; no real persons need to be exposed.

```
sealed public labeled sample + blocking and comparison settings
-> preserve source record IDs and original fields (pandas.DataFrame; pydantic)
-> build a linkage model with an explicit backend (splink.Linker; splink.DuckDBAPI)
-> train only on the declared training partition (Linker.training methods; settings as versioned data)
-> score candidate pairs (Linker.inference.predict)
-> route matches, nonmatches, and review candidates (P191 controlled threshold rules; clingo)
-> evaluate against held-out labels and record lineage (pandas joins; rdflib PROV-O)
-> pairwise candidate register + review queue + measured linkage report
```

contract: Blocking recall, pairwise precision/recall, cluster errors, and calibration are separate measures. A connected cluster does not prove all pairwise identities. True labels never enter matching features.

theoretical positive test: A noisy duplicate pair above the approved acceptance threshold is a match candidate; ambiguous pairs remain review candidates. Evaluation uses a label-separated holdout.

theoretical adverse test: Two unrelated records with the same name must not be merged by name alone. A-B and B-C similarity cannot bypass an A-C contradiction. An uncalibrated score cannot be described as certified identity.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for linkage evaluation and review routing. Identity proof and production error rates remain unproven.

public-data limit: Synthetic errors in S07 may differ substantially from client and legal-entity data. No production threshold can be inferred from its size or labels.


contract: The implication is shorthand for the exact declared predicates. Model checking covers the supplied abstraction only. Reject vacuous success when activation is unreachable unless that is the intended requirement.

theoretical positive test: The guarded fixture model reaches activation only after verification and authorization, and the property holds from all declared initial states.

theoretical adverse test: Add an activation edge that bypasses approval. The result must fail and provide a reachable violating state. An empty initial-state set cannot count as a meaningful pass.

public-data limit: Neither a public process log nor a formal model proves the real system enforces the modeled guards.

## P231  event lifecycles and approved responsibility mappings -> interval accounting -> attributable and unknown time

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U09 U14 U17
reuses: P12, P22, P58, P74, P210, P219
new capability: Hypothesis-generated interval mutations and PROV attribution over existing pandas/PM4Py events.
public basis: S09/S10 loan-application event-log descriptions; S06 simulated multi-object activity. Actor responsibility and client-wait mappings are authored test inputs.

```
P210 normalized events + P219 ordering + approved responsibility map
-> pair start, suspend, resume, and complete events by explicit work-instance keys (pandas.merge; PM4Py event fields; custom lifecycle adapter)
-> intersect intervals with the case observation window and union overlaps per category (datetime; sorted endpoint sweep)
-> partition elapsed time into internal-only, client-only, parallel, and unattributed intervals (custom interval algebra; pandas.groupby)
-> separately sum resource work intervals without labeling them elapsed time (pandas.groupby; fractions.Fraction)
-> mutate boundaries, overlaps, and missing markers (Hypothesis strategies; independent discretized small oracle)
-> publish source-linked time components and coverage (prov.ProvDocument; json.dumps)
```

contract: Half-open intervals and one time zone govern elapsed accounting. Parallel categories are separate; unique elapsed time must conserve the observation window. Resource-hours may exceed elapsed hours. Missing lifecycle markers prevent invented start or completion times.

theoretical positive test: Authored case window [0,10), internal intervals [0,4) and [2,6), client interval [5,8): internal-only=5, client-only=2, parallel=1, unattributed=2. Resource interval sum is 8; elapsed internal union is 6.

theoretical adverse test: Drop the start marker or introduce two possible matching work instances: affected time becomes unresolved. Repeating an identical event ID cannot increase attributed time; a distinct real work instance must remain.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for exact interval accounting. Public log descriptions support event-based testing; a defensible internal/client split requires the extra approved mapping and usable lifecycle fields.

public-data limit: Public resource labels do not establish whether time belongs to the client, the firm, or a waiting queue. Full public files and their marker coverage remain uninspected here.

required implementation and evidence: Implement instance pairing, provenance per interval, clock contracts, partition conservation, censored-boundary tests, and independent small interval enumeration.

## P232  open and completed cases -> right-censored duration model -> qualified remaining-time estimates

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U10 U11 U14
reuses: P21, P94, P211, P231
new capability: lifelines KaplanMeierFitter plus Hypothesis cohort and censoring tests.
public basis: S09/S10 historical loan events as a candidate duration/censoring source. Tutorial methods in L24 are public. Case closure and terminal outcomes require an explicit mapping.

```
case intake times + approved terminal outcome map + observation cutoff
-> construct durations and event_observed without turning open cases into completions (pandas; Pydantic strict types)
-> distinguish target completion, competing terminal events, and missing follow-up (custom cohort contract)
-> fit a declared right-censored cohort only when its censoring assumptions are defensible (lifelines.KaplanMeierFitter.fit)
-> derive conditional survival S(t+u)/S(t) where S(t)>0 and support is adequate (NumPy; explicit undefined states)
-> compare with an exact small risk-set product and test cutoffs (fractions.Fraction; Hypothesis)
-> record cohort, support, uncertainty, exclusions, and model version (prov; JSON)
```

contract: Completion, withdrawal, rejection, and right censoring have distinct meanings. Treating competing events as independent censoring requires justification; otherwise use a competing-risks extension. No tail extrapolation or finite median when the observed curve never crosses one half.

theoretical positive test: Authored durations [2,3,4] with event flags [true,false,true] produce survival 2/3 just after time 2, unchanged at censoring time 3, and zero after time 4 under the simple risk-set contract.

theoretical adverse test: An all-censored cohort cannot claim observed completion events or an observed median. A request beyond supported time, S(t)=0, or incomplete intake date produces unavailable rather than zero remaining time.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for qualified cohort estimates. This extends the retrospective clock proofs; transport to live onboarding and individual predictions needs separate validation.

public-data limit: The public event descriptions alone do not establish independent censoring, complete outcomes, stable cohorts, or the exact archive cutoff. They cannot certify forecast accuracy.

required implementation and evidence: Archive the log, reconcile actual cutoff, preregister cohorts/outcomes, test censoring and competing events, and backtest on later disjoint cohorts with coverage and errors.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: survival-cohort.json; survival-estimates.json; forecast-backtest.json.

Libraries and primary references: S09 S10 L24 L07 L17

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P233  explicit probabilistic model and observed evidence -> exact inference -> advisory diagnostic distributions

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U14 U16 U17
reuses: P95, P199, P211
new capability: pgmpy DiscreteBayesianNetwork and VariableElimination with independent rational enumeration.
public basis: S11 provides an explicitly parameterized public Bayesian-network example. A document-quality diagnostic network would be a separately labeled authored fixture, not a relabeling of those observations.

```
sealed model structure + conditional probability tables + typed observed evidence
-> validate state labels, DAG structure, table dimensions, and normalization (pgmpy.DiscreteBayesianNetwork.check_model; Pydantic)
-> retain missing observations as unobserved variables (custom evidence adapter)
-> calculate posterior distributions (pgmpy.inference.VariableElimination.query)
-> independently enumerate a small joint distribution (itertools.product; fractions.Fraction)
-> bind outputs to exact model and evidence versions (prov.ProvDocument; hashlib.sha256)
-> send advisory probabilities to a separate authorization gate (P199; Zen decision table)
```

contract: A posterior is conditional on the declared graph and parameters. It does not establish truth, legal status, wrongdoing, permission, or completed review. Impossible evidence with zero probability must be surfaced explicitly.

theoretical positive test: Authored two-state fixture: prior defect 1/10, signal sensitivity 4/5, false-positive rate 1/5. A positive signal gives posterior (4/50)/(13/50)=4/13. An absent signal observation leaves the prior 1/10.

theoretical adverse test: Non-normalized tables, unknown state labels, cycles, and zero-probability evidence are rejected or explicitly undefined. A 0.99 advisory score with absent approval cannot activate a case.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for model-based uncertainty handling. Exact inference can be checked against enumeration on small networks; meaningful operational probabilities need data and calibration.

public-data limit: The public teaching network supplies mathematical structure, not evidence about onboarding document defects or customers. No real-world diagnostic probability is estimated here.

required implementation and evidence: Archive public example parameters; test state ordering, table products, impossible evidence, model versioning, and strict separation of probabilistic and authorization outputs.

## P234  held-out labeled predictions -> calibration and selective review tests -> approved abstention policy

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U04 U14 U16
reuses: P201, P233, P199
new capability: scikit-learn calibration_curve and scoring; Hypothesis threshold-boundary tests.
public basis: S07 synthetic labeled linkage data is suitable for a linkage-score experiment. S11 can generate labeled samples from declared probabilities; neither supplies private document-review truth.

```
predictions + adjudicated labels + entity-group and time split register
-> keep training, calibration, threshold selection, and final test partitions separate (pandas; scikit-learn split utilities with group/time constraints)
-> compare score bins with observed frequencies and proper scores (sklearn.calibration.calibration_curve; sklearn.metrics.brier_score_loss)
-> compute error and coverage for an explicitly bounded abstention rule (NumPy; pandas.groupby)
-> evaluate subgroup support and confidence limits with case-level resampling (scipy.stats; NumPy random.Generator)
-> test exact cutoffs, missing labels, and unobserved classes (Hypothesis)
-> propose a review threshold requiring owner approval and a policy version (P199; prov)
```

contract: Brier loss combines several aspects of prediction quality and alone does not establish calibration. Linkage pairs sharing an entity must not leak across splits. Unlabeled examples cannot be counted as correct. Selective accuracy must be reported with retained coverage.

theoretical positive test: Authored predictions [0.2,0.8] and outcomes [0,1] have binary mean squared probability error 0.04. At a high-confidence threshold of 0.9, coverage is zero and selective accuracy is undefined.

theoretical adverse test: One true entity in both train and test is rejected by the split contract. An empty confidence bin, missing class, or tiny subgroup remains unsupported. Lower loss never automatically approves a production threshold.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for qualification of advisory scores and abstention. The key output is a supported error/coverage tradeoff with held-out evidence.

public-data limit: Synthetic linkage labels cannot establish document-extraction, sanctions-screening, or production reviewer accuracy. Pair sampling and prevalence affect apparent calibration.

required implementation and evidence: Implement case/entity grouping, frozen thresholds, independent score formulas, missing-label accounting, split hashes, and reviewer-approved deployment criteria.

## P235  proposed intervention and causal assumptions -> identification gate -> estimand or nonidentifiability report

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U14 U15
reuses: P46, P231, P233
new capability: DoWhy causal identification with explicit DAG assumptions and graph validation.
public basis: S12 is a publisher-simulated causal example with a declared generating effect. S09 is observational process data and is a candidate stress case for unsupported causal claims.

```
declared treatment + outcome + target population + causal assumption graph
-> validate names, temporal roles, and observed versus latent variables (Pydantic; networkx.is_directed_acyclic_graph)
-> construct the causal model (dowhy.CausalModel)
-> identify the effect under the recorded assumptions (CausalModel.identify_effect; noninteractive adapter with no silent confounding waiver)
-> inspect whether an admissible estimand exists before estimating (explicit identification-result contract)
-> check overlap and avoid post-treatment adjustment in the chosen design (pandas; custom variable-role checks)
-> produce an estimand with assumptions, or an unresolved identification record (prov; Jinja2)
```

contract: No automatic proceed-when-unidentifiable shortcut. Assumptions that cannot be established from the data stay explicit. A longest waiting-time edge is descriptive and does not establish the effect of automating that step.

theoretical positive test: Authored DAG Z->T, Z->Y, T->Y with observed pre-treatment Z admits a backdoor adjustment by Z under the graph assumptions. The output names the estimand and those assumptions before any estimate.

theoretical adverse test: Replace Z with an unobserved common cause and provide no valid instrument or frontdoor structure: the design must report the unsupported identification path rather than publish a causal benefit. Conditioning on a treatment-induced mediator changes the estimand and cannot be silent.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for identification discipline; PUBLIC_DATA_INSUFFICIENT to conclude real onboarding intervention benefits from the supplied public log descriptions.

public-data limit: Observed event order does not determine causal direction, absence of confounding, interference between cases, or the population targeted by a staffing intervention.

required implementation and evidence: Test identifiable and nonidentifiable graphs, observed-variable mapping, latent confounding, selection bias, and explicit assumptions without interactive runtime interpretation.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: causal-question.json; identified-estimand.json or identification-gap.json.

## P236  identified intervention model -> estimates and sensitivity -> conditional benefit evidence

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U14 U15 U17
reuses: P235, P225, P227
new capability: DoWhy estimation and refutation composed with independent synthetic-effect checks.
public basis: S12 supplies a public simulated linear-data generator with beta=10 in its worked example. Future local samples must record generator settings, seed, and exact data bytes.

```
P235 identified estimand + compatible data + estimator specification
-> fit only the estimator permitted by the identification contract (dowhy.CausalModel.estimate_effect)
-> preserve target population and uncertainty method (typed estimate adapter; pandas)
-> run placebo, added-common-cause, and declared sensitivity checks (CausalModel.refute_estimate; explicit supported methods)
-> compare simulated samples with their known generating effect using prespecified statistical acceptance (NumPy; scipy.stats)
-> translate a supported effect into a conditional operating scenario with all conversions exposed (P225; decimal.Decimal)
-> record estimate, uncertainty, refutation outcomes, and residual assumptions (prov; JSON)
```

contract: Passing refutation tests does not prove all causal assumptions. Finite-sample estimates need not equal the generating coefficient exactly. Deterministic pass/fail thresholds and seeds must be set before inspecting results.

theoretical positive test: On the public generator, beta=10 is the declared target for an average-effect experiment. A separate noise-free authored fixture Y=10*T+3*Z verifies an adjusted coefficient of 10 when the design matrix has full rank.

theoretical adverse test: An omitted confounder, absent overlap, post-treatment feature leakage, or effect interval spanning both benefit and harm blocks a definitive positive benefit claim. Random-placebo failure is retained, not rerun until a favorable seed appears.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for auditable scenario evidence. A controlled prospective evaluation would still be needed to support a claim about a new onboarding process.

public-data limit: The synthetic coefficient is a known mathematical input. It is unrelated to any private cycle-time or revenue objective. Public historical application data alone cannot prove the proposed intervention effect.

required implementation and evidence: Implement estimator-selection contracts, seed registry, refutation and sensitivity results, confidence-interval checks, repeated-sample coverage evaluation, and conversion provenance.

## P238  formal adapter contract and bounded grammar -> synthesized expression -> independent counterexample check

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U02 U16 U18
reuses: P191, P197, P198
new capability: cvc5 syntax-guided synthesis, checked independently with Z3 and enumerated boundary oracles.
public basis: L29 is a public synthesis example. S01 minimum-membership threshold supplies a small public rule shape; its actual schema and exception language remain governed by P191.

```
approved typed function specification + allowed grammar + input domain
-> encode a synthesis conjecture without external calls or mutable state (cvc5 Solver; mkGrammar; synthFun; addSygusConstraint)
-> request a candidate and retain solution, no-solution, or unknown status (Solver.checkSynth)
-> extract only grammar-permitted typed expressions (Solver.getSynthSolution; custom restricted AST adapter)
-> substitute the candidate into the independent specification and seek a counterexample (z3.Solver.check on domain AND NOT specification)
-> enumerate a finite witness domain and reject invalid input coercions (itertools; Pydantic; Hypothesis)
-> register the candidate as a reviewed versioned adapter, never self-deploy it (hashlib; P199; prov)
```

contract: The grammar and formal specification define the claim. A finite test gives a bounded result; an unsat counterexample query can prove the encoded property over its stated domain. Unknown is unverified. No arbitrary Python execution of generated text.

theoretical positive test: For integer n>=0 and a specification result iff n>=4, a candidate n>=4 must agree at n=0,3,4,5 and have no counterexample in the encoded domain. The candidate n>4 has witness n=4.

theoretical adverse test: An expression that calls an external function, changes the input domain, omits a missing-value route, or relies on solver unknown is rejected. A malformed normative translation remains malformed even when synthesis succeeds.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for small adapters and decision expressions. This is a bounded synthesis research track, not automatic production policy authoring.

public-data limit: The public rule provides a simple threshold only. It cannot prove synthesis of whole legal texts, arbitrary transformations, or the correct organizational interpretation of exceptions.

required implementation and evidence: Pin the cvc5/Z3 API versions, preserve grammar/specification/candidate hashes, prove adapter semantics, and test a deliberately erroneous candidate with a recorded counterexample.

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**


contract: Durable execution requires a service and workers. Workflow determinism, activity idempotency, business outcome verification, and authorization are separate obligations. Recorded success of an activity cannot establish a policy interpretation.

theoretical positive test: Adapt a public hello-activity example into an authored submit/review gate. A restart after recorded review must retain that decision and the same pending next action when the identical history is replayed.

theoretical adverse test: An unversioned workflow change that schedules a different command for the same history must fail replay qualification. A missing activity result or approval remains pending; a direct current-time or network read in workflow decision code is rejected by the design contract.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for long-lived case orchestration. The service deployment, selected SDK, and business adapters need actual integration and fault tests.

## P242  approved action intent and retries -> outbox, inbox, and receipt reconciliation -> duplicate-safe effects

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U06 U12 U16 U17
reuses: P199, P210, P241
new capability: Temporal retries plus transactional outbox/inbox adapters and Hypothesis fault sequences.
public basis: S14 retry samples and L33 idempotency guidance. External providers and receipts are replaced by clearly labeled local service simulators for theoretical fault cases.

```
authorized action intent + stable semantic action ID + expected state version
-> commit intent and local state atomically (sqlite3.Connection transaction; UNIQUE action_id; transactional outbox)
-> dispatch with an idempotency key bound to destination, payload, and logical action (Temporal activity; fixed adapter)
-> reconcile timeout/unknown outcomes with the destination receipt contract before retry policy decides (typed status query; activity retry rules)
-> reject reused keys with different payloads and deduplicate incoming receipts (hashlib; transactional inbox)
-> inject crashes before commit, after send, after remote commit, and before acknowledgment (Hypothesis state machine; pytest service doubles)
-> publish committed, pending, duplicate, conflicting, and unknown outcomes separately (prov; JSON)
```

contract: A local unique key does not make a remote effect exactly-once. The destination must honor the key or offer a safe reconciliation protocol. No definitive completed status without an outcome receipt. Intent atomicity covers only its actual transaction boundary.

theoretical positive test: An authored destination stores receipts by action ID. A lost acknowledgment followed by the same intent must yield one destination effect and the same receipt. Duplicate inbound receipts leave one committed local transition.

theoretical adverse test: A provider without idempotency or outcome lookup returns unknown after a post-send timeout and routes to reconciliation. Reusing a key for altered account attributes is a conflict, never a cached success.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT when each destination supports the required protocol; PARTIAL_FIT where outcomes cannot be reconciled safely.

public-data limit: The public examples do not establish the guarantees of actual onboarding APIs or their retention period for idempotency keys. Local simulation alone cannot prove remote exactly-once behavior.

required implementation and evidence: Implement payload-bound keys, durable transaction tests, remote simulator fault injection, real provider contract verification, receipt retention, and duplicate/conflict accounting.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: action-intents.json; reconciled-receipts.json; retry-fault-tests.xml.

Libraries and primary references: S14 L33 L31 L07 L17

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.

theoretical adverse test: A document already delivered cannot be made undelivered. Its remedy is a separately authorized correction or withdrawal process. A failed compensation stays unresolved and cannot create a fully rolled-back flag.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for explicit recovery in distributed lifecycle execution. This strengthens the legacy reversed-step presentation into a separately verified recovery mechanism.

## P244  verified proposal and changing case state -> freshness fence -> authorized dispatch or stale rejection

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U04 U12 U16
reuses: P199, P211, P214, P218, P242

```

-> validate the submitted message without mutating workflow state (Temporal update validator; Pydantic)
-> reevaluate evidence freshness, withdrawal, actor authority, and policy at dispatch (P199; P211; fixed clock contract)
-> atomically bind intent to the checked local version (SQL UPDATE WHERE version=expected; outbox transaction)

-> model and test approve/revoke/dispatch interleavings (Z3 bounded transition model; Hypothesis)
-> record accepted, stale, denied, and remote-fence-unavailable outcomes (prov; JSON)
```

contract: A preflight check alone cannot eliminate a check/use race. The dispatch fence must cover the actual mutation boundary. A local transaction cannot fence an independent remote service unless the protocol supports that contract.

theoretical positive test: Authored case version1 permits a review proposal. A withdrawal moves the case to version2 before dispatch; a compare-and-swap expecting version1 changes zero rows and creates no authorized activation intent.

theoretical adverse test: Concurrent approval and withdrawal without a defined order must not select whichever event arrives conveniently. If a destination lacks a required conditional mutation, flag the remaining race rather than claim atomic end-to-end authorization.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for version-fenced execution; unresolved external race conditions remain explicit deployment blockers.

public-data limit: Public handler documentation supplies API behavior, not authority or atomicity guarantees across the private system estate.

required implementation and evidence: Test all bounded interleavings, validator nonmutation, stale tokens, expiry boundaries, revoked evidence, provider conditional writes, and atomic outbox behavior.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for controlled evolution of long-lived cases. Each schema and workflow version pair needs explicit tests.

public-data limit: Public example histories do not cover the private status vocabulary or all future version combinations. Generic JSON compatibility is weaker than semantic compatibility.

```
-> derive the full receiving-member requirement set independently (P200; clingo; Z3)
-> test each existing evidence item for identity, purpose, freshness, and reliance permission (Casbin; P205)
-> partition requirements into reusable, new, conflicting, and unresolved sets (RDFLib; pySHACL)
-> construct an authorized candidate plan for only the outstanding obligations (Unified Planning; P221; separate authority check)
-> validate receiving-party agreements and configuration dependencies without inheriting old approvals (P204; P244)
-> export the entity-add package and explanations back to original case and rule records (prov; Jinja2; JSON)
```

contract: Every receiving-member requirement appears exactly once in the partition. A reused document can satisfy evidence needs only under explicit permission. Prior-case approval, signed-agreement parties, and activation state never transfer merely because client identity matches.

theoretical positive test: For an authored receiving manifest of five obligations, two eligible evidence items produce two reusable and three outstanding obligations. The prior member stays unchanged; the new member cannot activate until its three obligations and current approvals are evidenced.

theoretical adverse test: Revoke reliance permission for one of the two documents: the new-work set grows to four. A prior agreement with a different receiving party remains insufficient even when its title and terms appear identical.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for the entity-add lifecycle as a composed resolver, reuse, planning, and readiness contract.

public-data limit: Public profile and contracting formats establish mechanics. They supply no permission to rely on a private KYC assessment or enforceability judgment for a receiving-party agreement.

required implementation and evidence: Bind owner-approved reliance rules to exact scopes, implement partition conservation tests, validate plans independently, and qualify a real receiving-member integration in a separate authorized environment.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: entity-add-manifest.json; reuse-decisions.json; outstanding-plan.json; receiving-member-gates.json.

```
raw decision JSON + versioned numeric/string profile + canonicalization standard identifier
-> reject duplicate keys, nonfinite extensions, invalid Unicode, and unsupported input types before information loss (json object_pairs_hook; strict typed decoder)
-> encode exact decimal/rational fields by the declared schema without silent binary-float conversion (Decimal; Fraction; Pydantic)
-> canonicalize only supported values with the selected standard implementation (rfc8785.dumps; explicit domain-error handling)
-> compute separate source-byte and canonical-envelope hashes (hashlib.sha256; P17)
-> sign and verify the canonical envelope while retaining scope and authority checks (cryptography; P247; Casbin)
-> compare standard vectors and boundary cases with an independent implementation (pytest; Hypothesis; provenance manifest)
```

contract: Sorted keys from json.dumps do not establish RFC 8785 conformance. Unicode normalization is a separate transformation and cannot silently change signed strings. Decimal strings need an explicit scale/value contract; source-byte identity and semantic-equivalence claims are separate.

theoretical positive test: Equivalent property orderings within the supported profile produce identical canonical bytes. RFC vectors must agree byte for byte across implementations. An exact decimal represented by the approved schema remains exact after roundtrip and signature verification.

theoretical adverse test: Duplicate allow keys are rejected before last-value-wins parsing. Unsupported large integers, NaN, unpaired surrogates, and forbidden numeric coercions fail. A Unicode ordering counterexample must expose a naive code-point sorter that differs from the required ordering.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for portable decision-envelope signatures and explicitly defined fingerprints.

public-data limit: The current bounded tests exercise a restricted local JSON profile and a Unicode-order counterexample. They do not run rfc8785 or establish cross-language interoperability.

required implementation and evidence: Pin both independent implementations, archive public vectors, define exact numeric encodings, and run invalid-input and signature-binding tests before adopting a canonical envelope contract.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: canonical-envelope.bin; source-and-envelope-hashes.json; interoperability-results.json; signature-envelope.json.

## P271  source-bound contradiction -> checked irreducible subset -> smaller conflict explanation with explicit minimality status

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

## P276  typed service dependencies and uncertain failure rates -> Boolean failure model -> scenario bounds with dependence explicit

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U06 U11 U12 U14 U15
reuses: P207 typed interfaces; P229 stress tests; P257 readiness; P273 diagrams
new capability: SymPy Boolean formulas + Fraction scenario evaluation + SciPy linear-program bounds

```
source-bound service dependency types + declared failure formula + probability assumptions
-> distinguish all-required services, alternatives, and shared dependencies (Pydantic; NetworkX; explicit AND/OR semantics)
-> compile and simplify the Boolean failure event without duplicating shared causes (SymPy And/Or/simplify_logic; optional BDD)
-> evaluate joint worlds under an explicitly supplied dependence model (Fraction; itertools.product; pgmpy when qualified)
-> when only marginals are known, optimize event probability across feasible joint masses (scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs"))
-> verify probability conservation, marginal constraints, feasibility, and numerical tolerance (NumPy; independent sums; solver status)
-> record scenario assumptions, lower/upper bounds, and missing failure-mode coverage (prov; JSON)
```

contract: Graph reachability alone does not define system failure. Independence is an assumption that must be declared. Known marginal failure rates generally leave a range for a compound event. Exact rational reference values and floating solver results keep separate precision descriptions. Unmodeled common causes remain a model limit.

theoretical positive test: For authored event probabilities A=0.1, B=0.2, C=0.05 and failure C OR (A AND B), independent joint enumeration gives 69/1000. With only those marginals, an eight-world linear program gives bounds [0.05,0.15]. The local SciPy result must satisfy all mass and marginal constraints.

theoretical adverse test: Adding failure probabilities as if events were disjoint, multiplying them without an independence assumption, double-counting a shared provider, or accepting negative/inconsistent joint masses fails. A solver failure leaves bounds unresolved.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for transparent resilience and capacity scenarios with explicit dependence uncertainty.

public-data limit: The published event logs and scheduling examples do not supply operational outage rates, causal failure independence, or complete dependency semantics. The bounded local calculation is an authored scenario, not an estimated production reliability figure.

## P278  four-state evidence rules -> paired Boolean rails -> cross-engine semantic checks without unknown-value collapse

contract: For this declared algebra, negation swaps rails; conjunction uses (t1 AND t2, f1 OR f2); disjunction uses (t1 OR t2, f1 AND f2). Applicability and authorization remain separate dimensions. theoretical positive test: All four unary negations and sixteen ordered binary input pairs match the independent truth table. Double negation and the declared De Morgan identities hold. theoretical adverse test: Casting unknown to Python False, erasing refutation once support appears, rewriting every p OR NOT p to supported, or allowing an unsupported temporal/deontic operator through an unqualified adapter fails. Engine agreement without the independent table is insufficient.

## P280  review population and observed labels -> qualified sample assessment -> uncertainty-aware quality report

## P283  event timestamps and clock uncertainty -> interval order constraints -> honest conformance and deadline outcomes

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U09 U11 U13 U17
reuses: P219 partial event order; P224 calendars; P231 time attribution; P218 temporal monitoring
new capability: intervaltree indexing + explicit closed-bound adapter + Z3 interval constraints
public basis: S06 and S09 provide candidate event-log formats. Neither supplies verified device-clock error bounds for the private process. Timestamp errors and interval bounds in the reference tests are authored assumptions.

```
events with observed timestamps + clock-source identities + explicit uncertainty bounds + precedence requirements
-> normalize known time zones and retain the original timestamp precision (datetime; dateutil; P224)
-> derive a possible true-time interval only from supplied clock bounds (Pydantic; exact integer-time arithmetic)
-> index overlaps through a tested conversion to the library's half-open interval convention (intervaltree.IntervalTree; explicit endpoint contract)
-> assert only event orders that hold throughout the supplied bounds (Z3 inequalities; P219)
-> classify deadline satisfaction as certain, impossible, or unresolved under the interval and boundary policy (RTAMT adapter or exact interval oracle)
-> report nominal order separately from supported order, with clock gaps and source references (PM4Py input adapter; prov)
```

contract: Closed uncertainty bounds describe possible instants. Strict A-before-B is established when the upper bound of A is below the lower bound of B. An overlap leaves the order undecided unless other trusted evidence constrains it. A clock bound is an assumption or measurement with provenance, not a confidence interval unless explicitly justified. No uncertainty is invented when absent.

theoretical positive test: Authored intervals A=[98,102] and B=[101,105] leave their true order unresolved despite ordered nominal times. [0,1] is strictly before [2,3]. Completion [90,100] meets an inclusive deadline 100; [99,101] remains unresolved.

theoretical adverse test: Using ingest order or nominal timestamps to certify an ambiguous sequence fails. Closed [4,4] must not disappear when adapted to a half-open index. Reversed bounds, unsupported units, unknown zones, or missing clock evidence block the relevant comparison.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for event conformance that accounts for clock and precision limits.

public-data limit: Public event descriptions establish timestamp fields, not clock calibration or causal order. The local suite checks exact interval arithmetic only. intervaltree, RTAMT, Z3, and full PM4Py composition remain unexecuted.

required implementation and evidence: Obtain clock and precision contracts, implement endpoint conversion with overflow checks, compare interval results against an independent oracle, and preserve unresolved orders in every downstream conformance report.

## P287  probabilistic workflow model -> reachability and reward properties -> conditional completion bounds

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U11 U12 U14 U17
reuses: P217 liveness; P225 simulation; P229 stress; P276 dependence bounds
new capability: stormpy probabilistic model checking + explicit stochastic model + independent linear-equation oracle
public basis: S26 supplies a public PRISM probabilistic-model example and L61 Python bindings. The review/retry/ready/reject chain is authored. No transition probability is inferred from an inter-event gap or imported from an unrelated public process.

```
finite stochastic workflow + justified transition probabilities + terminal-state and time-unit definitions

-> compare scenario results with simulation only under the same assumptions and horizon (SimPy; P225; prov)
```

contract: DTMC steps are discrete transitions, not business days unless the model defines that relationship. A Markov assumption and stationary probabilities require justification. For an MDP, min/max results depend on the scheduler class and cannot silently become a single realized forecast. Nonabsorbing states and infinite expected times remain explicit.

theoretical positive test: In the authored chain, each step reaches ready with probability 1/2, retries with 1/4, and rejects with 1/4. Eventual ready probability is 2/3; expected time to either absorbing outcome is 4/3 steps; ready within two steps is 5/8. Independent Fraction equations and actual SciPy solves agree.

theoretical adverse test: Negative probabilities, rows that do not sum to one, mislabeled terminal states, reward units treated as days without a mapping, or a closed nonabsorbing component hidden from the output fails. A model probability must never be presented as an observed private completion rate.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for mathematically explicit completion and resilience scenarios, with empirical calibration as a separate requirement.

public-data limit: The public die model demonstrates model-checker mechanics. It says nothing about onboarding probabilities. The local suite solves a tiny authored chain; stormpy and a complete stochastic-process adapter were not executed.

## P290  verified derivation and dependency envelope -> guarded cache reuse -> fast replay without stale authority

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U02 U04 U15 U16 U17 U18
reuses: P17 hashes; P211 bitemporal state; P212 impact; P244 version fence; P262 canonical envelopes
new capability: DiskCache persistent bytes + content-addressed dependency keys + current authority and freshness rechecks
public basis: S02 offers a public versioned schedule analogue and S05 versioned records. L65 documents cache behavior. Dependency keys, stale entries, authority changes, and corrupt payloads are authored fixtures.

```
pure derivation inputs + schema/compiler/rule versions + case scope + evidence and authority versions
-> enumerate every declared dependency and effective/known-at snapshot used by the derivation (Pydantic; prov; P211)
-> construct a canonical content-addressed key including namespace and semantic profile (P262; hashlib.sha256)
-> store only validated bytes and a trusted dependency/integrity envelope (diskcache.Cache.set; explicit serialization policy)
-> retrieve through one wrapper that checks context equality, validity, integrity, and current audience permission (Cache.get; Casbin; P244)
-> recompute on miss, stale or changed dependency, failed write, or unverifiable provenance (versioned pure function; P212)
-> retain cache outcome and independently recheck authorization immediately before any side effect (Temporal activity gate; prov)
```

contract: Caching accelerates a derivation. It cannot grant authority or establish fresh evidence. TTL does not replace rule-effective dates or revocation checks. A complete key requires a reviewed dependency inventory; a hash cannot detect an omitted dependency. Untrusted pickle is excluded. Cache and FanoutCache write/transaction outcomes must not be assumed identical.

theoretical positive test: Changing any of eleven authored dependency fields changes the key, while reordering the same envelope fields does not. A valid entry is reused only before its declared validity boundary with current permission and the trusted expected payload hash.

theoretical adverse test: A changed tenant, entity, rule, evidence, compiler, or authority version misses the old key. At the exact expiration boundary the entry is stale. Permission revocation denies reuse. Changed payload bytes with an unchanged trusted hash produce corruption. A failed cache write cannot be reported as durable success.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for efficient deterministic replay that preserves evidence and authority boundaries.

public-data limit: The local suite checks a Python dictionary cache wrapper and key envelope. DiskCache, concurrent writers, process crashes, and complete dependency discovery were not executed or qualified. No speedup or private-program cache safety is claimed.

required implementation and evidence: Implement a reviewed dependency schema, use safe bytes-only serialization, test concurrent and failed writes for the selected backend, and compare cached versus uncached results across policy and permission changes.

planned outputs, not created by this assessment: derivation-cache-envelope.json; dependency-key-tests.json; cache-outcome-log.json; cached-vs-fresh-parity.json; revoked-entry-tests.json.

Libraries and primary references: S02 S05 L10 L17 L31 L37 L44 L65

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.

```python
"""Bounded reference checks. These do not execute or qualify the full P191+ chains.
Run: python reference_checks.py --report checks/reference-results.json
The only external inputs are the transcribed samples in sources/reference-web-samples.json.
Other inputs are explicit test fixtures defined here. No network or external actions are used.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal
from fractions import Fraction as F
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import importlib.util
import itertools
import json
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import sqlite3
import traceback
import unicodedata
from typing import Any, Callable, Literal
from lark import Lark, UnexpectedInput
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError
import networkx as nx
from rdflib import Graph, URIRef, Literal as RDFLiteral, Namespace
from rdflib.compare import isomorphic
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
import numpy as np
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PublicKey

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
INPUT_PATH = ROOT / 'sources/reference-web-samples.json'
INPUTS = json.loads(INPUT_PATH.read_text())
CASES: list[tuple[str, tuple[int, ...], Callable[[], dict[str, Any]]]] = []
ASSERTIONS = 0

def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    global ASSERTIONS
    ASSERTIONS += 1
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)

def equal(actual: Any, expected: Any) -> None:
    require(actual == expected, f'{actual!r} != {expected!r}')

def rejects(exc: type[BaseException], fn: Callable[[], Any]) -> None:
    try:
        fn()
    except exc:
        require(True, 'expected exception')
    else:
        require(False, f'Expected {exc.__name__}')

def case(*proofs: int):
    def register(fn):
        CASES.append((fn.__name__, proofs, fn))
        return fn
    return register

def canonical(x: Any) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode()

def digest(b: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()

class Membership(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, extra='forbid')
    voting_members: int = Field(ge=0)

GRAMMAR = r'''
start: MODAL ACTOR ACTION OBJECT "when" FIELD OP INT
MODAL: "require" | "permit" | "forbid"
ACTOR: /[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*/
ACTION: /[a-z][a-z_]*/
OBJECT: /[a-z][a-z_]*/
FIELD: /[a-z][a-z_]*/
OP: ">=" | ">" | "=="
%import common.INT
%import common.WS
%ignore WS
'''
PARSER = Lark(GRAMMAR, parser='lalr')

def parse_controlled(s: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    t = PARSER.parse(s)
    v = [str(x) for x in t.children]
    return dict(zip(('modality','actor','action','object','field','operator','threshold'), v)) | {'threshold':int(v[-1])}

@case(191,197)

    equal([r['modality'] for r in rows],['require','permit','forbid'])
    equal({r['threshold'] for r in rows},{4})
    require(rows[0] != rows[2], 'require and forbid collapsed')
    return {'parsed':3,'modality_values':[r['modality'] for r in rows]}

@case(222,239)
def public_jobshop_exhaustive_machine_orders():
    jobs=INPUTS['jobshop']['jobs'];tasks={};machines=defaultdict(list);base=nx.DiGraph()
    for j,ops in enumerate(jobs):
        for k,(m,p) in enumerate(ops):
            key=(j,k);tasks[key]=(m,p);machines[m].append(key);base.add_node(key)
            if k:base.add_edge((j,k-1),key)
    considered=0;acyclic=0;best=None;best_rows=None
    permutations=[list(itertools.permutations(machines[m])) for m in sorted(machines)]
    for orders in itertools.product(*permutations):
        considered+=1;g=base.copy()
        for order in orders:g.add_edges_from(zip(order,order[1:]))
        if not nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(g):continue
        acyclic+=1;finish={};rows=[]
        for t in nx.lexicographical_topological_sort(g):
            start=max((finish[p] for p in g.predecessors(t)),default=0)
            finish[t]=start+tasks[t][1]
            rows.append({'job':t[0],'task':t[1],'machine':tasks[t][0],'start':start,'end':finish[t]})
        makespan=max(finish.values())
        if best is None or makespan<best:best=makespan;best_rows=rows
    equal(considered,72);equal(best,INPUTS['jobshop']['published_optimum']);equal(len(tasks),8)
    require(0<acyclic<considered,'acyclic/cyclic classification failed')
    # Independent interval-level readback of the best assignment.
    lookup={(r['job'],r['task']):r for r in best_rows}
    for t,(m,p) in tasks.items():
        equal(lookup[t]['end']-lookup[t]['start'],p)
        if t[1]:require(lookup[(t[0],t[1]-1)]['end']<=lookup[t]['start'],'precedence breach')
    for a,b in itertools.combinations(best_rows,2):
        if a['machine']==b['machine']:
            require(a['end']<=b['start'] or b['end']<=a['start'],'machine overlap')
    return {'all_machine_orders':considered,'acyclic_orders':acyclic,'cyclic_orders':considered-acyclic,'proven_minimum_for_this_model':best,'schedule':best_rows,'ortools_executed':False}

@case(227,229)
def pareto_frontier_retains_tradeoffs_and_hard_gates():
    rows={'a':(4,8,True),'b':(6,6,True),'c':(7,9,True),'unsafe':(1,1,False)}
    good={k:v[:2] for k,v in rows.items() if v[2]}

@case(235,236)
def confounding_changes_naive_but_not_adjusted_toy_effect():
    # Full-rank, deliberately unbalanced, noise-free fixture Y=10*T+3*Z.
    records=[(0,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1),(1,1)]
    x=np.array([[1,t,z] for t,z in records],dtype=float)
    y=np.array([10*t+3*z for t,z in records],dtype=float)
    coeff,_,rank,_=np.linalg.lstsq(x,y,rcond=None)
    require(rank==3,'rank-deficient fixture')
    require(np.allclose(coeff,[0,10,3],atol=1e-10),'known generating coefficients not recovered')
    naive=float(np.mean([v for v,(t,z) in zip(y,records) if t])-np.mean([v for v,(t,z) in zip(y,records) if not t]))
    equal(naive,11.0)
    return {'generating_effect':10,'adjusted_coefficient':round(float(coeff[1]),10),'naive_difference':naive,'dowhy_identification_executed':False}

@case(242,244)
def transaction_idempotency_and_compare_and_swap():
    with sqlite3.connect(':memory:') as db:
        db.execute('CREATE TABLE state(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, version INTEGER, value TEXT)')
        db.execute('CREATE TABLE inbox(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT)')
        db.execute("INSERT INTO state VALUES('c',1,'review')")
        db.execute("INSERT INTO inbox VALUES('event1','same')")
        db.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO inbox VALUES('event1','same')")
        equal(db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inbox').fetchone()[0],1)
        changed=db.execute("UPDATE state SET value='approved',version=2 WHERE id='c' AND version=1").rowcount
        equal(changed,1)
        stale=db.execute("UPDATE state SET value='active',version=3 WHERE id='c' AND version=1").rowcount
        equal(stale,0)
        equal(db.execute('SELECT version,value FROM state').fetchone(),(2,'approved'))
    return {'duplicate_rows':1,'first_cas_updated':1,'stale_cas_updated':0,'external_exactly_once_proven':False}

@case(247)
def public_signature_vectors_verify_and_mutations_fail():
    vectors=INPUTS['ed25519']['vectors']

def run_suite() -> dict[str, Any]:
    global ASSERTIONS
    ASSERTIONS=0;records=[]
    for name,proofs,fn in CASES:
        before=ASSERTIONS
        try:
            evidence=fn();status='passed';error=None
        except Exception:
            evidence={};status='failed';error=traceback.format_exc()
        records.append({'id':name,'proof_requirements':list(proofs),'status':status,'assertions':ASSERTIONS-before,'evidence':evidence,'error':error})
    used=['lark','pydantic','networkx','rdflib','jsonschema','numpy','python-dateutil','cryptography']
    versions={n:importlib.metadata.version(n) for n in used}
    probe={n:importlib.util.find_spec(n) is not None for n in ['pyshacl','z3','clingo','hypothesis','simpy','ortools','duckdb','pm4py','prov','cvc5','temporalio','pgmpy','dowhy','river','lifelines','clips']}
    return {'scope':'Bounded reference checks only. No complete proposed P191+ library chain is executed or promoted.',
      'public_input_scope':'Three manually transcribed public samples: charter minimum, job-shop example, RFC 8032 signature vectors. All other data are authored fixtures.',
      'python_version':platform.python_version(),'used_library_versions':versions,
      'optional_import_probe':probe,'source_code_sha256':digest(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
      'input_sha256':digest(INPUT_PATH.read_bytes()),'input_path':'sources/reference-web-samples.json',
      'reference_cases':len(records),'passed':sum(x['status']=='passed' for x in records),
      'failed':sum(x['status']=='failed' for x in records),'assertions':ASSERTIONS,
      'full_chains_executed':0,'public_complete_datasets_ingested':0,
      'live_business_actions':0,'results':records}

if __name__=='__main__':
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);p.add_argument('--report',type=Path,default=ROOT/'checks/reference-results.json');args=p.parse_args()
    report=run_suite();args.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False,sort_keys=True)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ['reference_cases','passed','failed','assertions','full_chains_executed']},indent=2))
    if report['failed']:
        for r in report['results']:
            if r['status']=='failed':print(r['id'],r['error'])
        raise SystemExit(1)
```

## Extension batch 11: Ownership cycles, policy composition, evidence acquisition, and qualified data boundaries

Added September 7, 2026. This batch adds exactly P291-P300 to the complete P1-P290 master. The preceding text, recovery amendment, and embedded historical code remain unchanged. Earlier statements about the number of proofs or available implementations describe their own checkpoints.

Evidence categories remain separate. The ten complete chains below are SPECIFIED_NOT_EXECUTED. The embedded reference program executes bounded portions using installed libraries and explicit fixtures. Its results, source code, input projections, and the first-run correction record are included in this same TXT. A passed reference case does not qualify a complete chain or authorize a business action.

Public specifications and official library documentation were reviewed for this batch. Public samples are small manually transcribed projections of the cited examples. No complete external dataset or private case population was acquired. All invented case identities, ownership shares, provider replies, approval states, costs, and privacy budgets are labeled authored fixtures. The actual package versions used by the bounded tests are recorded with their results. Proposed dependencies are not asserted installed.
