## P291  cyclic economic interests -> exact simultaneous equations -> bounded participation and unresolved ownership blocks

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U07 U08 U10 U17
reuses: P202 relationship typing; P211 dated facts; P253 direct/component distinction and acyclic look-through; P282 exact quantities
new capability: SymPy rational matrix solving inside NetworkX strongly connected components, with independent Fraction residual checks and optional Z3 feasibility constraints
public basis: S17 and L39 define BODS relationship/component representation. L66 supplies an exact linear-equation method. BODS does not prescribe the economic recursion below. Its equation, completeness assumptions, and cyclic share values are an authored analytical model.

```
dated direct economic interests + explicit share-class contract + external-holder register
-> validate issuer/holder orientation, rational shares, source versions, and component identities (Pydantic; RDFLib; P253)
-> identify cyclic blocks without flattening them into repeated paths (networkx.strongly_connected_components; condensation)
-> define C[owner_company, issuer_company] and x = d + transpose(C)*x for the approved linear economic model (sympy.Matrix; Rational)
-> require a declared convergence certificate and nonsingular I-transpose(C), then solve each supported block (Matrix.det; LUsolve)
-> independently verify equations, bounds, and any claimed external-holder conservation (fractions.Fraction; optional Z3 constraints)
-> return source-linked economic participation or unresolved blocks, retaining all control and ownership declarations separately (prov; JSON)
```

contract: This extends P253 only for the stated linear economic-interest model. It never changes that proof's acyclic contract. Voting rights, effective control, beneficial-owner disclosure, treasury shares, and legal interpretation require separate approved models. Missing interests are not zero. A sufficient conservative qualification condition is a nonnegative C with every column sum below one. Blocks outside that condition require another justified certificate or remain unsupported. A numerical pseudoinverse must not manufacture a unique result for a singular block.

theoretical positive test: In the authored model, A owns half of B, B owns one quarter of A, and person P directly owns half of A. The equations give P economic participation of 4/7 in A and 2/7 in B. A separately declared external holder owns the remaining direct shares; the two computed holder vectors sum to one for each issuer.

theoretical adverse test: A closed pair with reciprocal 100-percent company holdings makes I-transpose(C) singular and stays unresolved. An unknown percentage, duplicate component, conflicting effective version, incompatible share class, or negative share blocks the affected result. An indirect summary must not be added to its components.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for exact cyclic economic calculations under an approved, complete linear model. It addresses a deliberately excluded case in P253 without treating algebra as a beneficial-owner determination.

public-data limit: The ownership graph and shares are authored. Public BODS examples establish representation mechanics only. No real circular ownership network, control conclusion, or institution-specific disclosure threshold is verified.

required implementation and evidence: Implement the pinned BODS adapter, approved economic convention, convergence gate, per-block source lineage, and independent conservation checks. Qualify incomplete and near-boundary blocks before extending the supported domain.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: cyclic-economic-interests.json; equation-residuals.json; unresolved-ownership-blocks.json; declared-versus-derived-interests.json.

Libraries and primary references: S17 L39 L04 L17 L66

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P292  inherited permissions and prohibitions -> explicit conflict strategy -> policy-composition result with outstanding duties

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U02 U03 U04 U06 U07 U16
reuses: P191 controlled semantics; P193 scoped contradictions; P206 authorization; P260 commonality; P265 offline reference registry
new capability: Pinned ODRL vocabulary and optional OWL-RL action closure composed with RDFLib, pySHACL, and clingo policy evaluation
public basis: S27 defines permission/prohibition conflicts, action inclusion, inheritance, and strategy terms perm, prohibit, and invalid. The default strategy is invalid. The test's action graph and actor/evidence envelopes are explicit projections or authored fixtures.

```
sealed policies + approved ODRL profile + action vocabulary + authenticated request context
-> load inherited policies from the sealed registry and reject missing parents or inheritance cycles in the supported profile (RDFLib; P265; NetworkX)
-> separate asserted action relationships from allowed entailed relationships (owlrl.DeductiveClosure; OWLRL_Semantics; graph difference)
-> expand compact rules and validate target, party, profile, duty, and conflict properties (pyshacl.validate; explicit ODRL adapter)
-> find scoped permission/prohibition conflicts, including encompassing actions (clingo; P193; typed action closure)
-> apply the declared profile conflict strategy and keep policy validity separate from duty fulfillment (versioned rule evaluator; P199)
-> recheck actual actor authority before recording an executable authorization (Casbin; P206; prov)
```

contract: ODRL expresses a policy chosen by an authorized owner. It cannot determine which private policy is legally controlling. Unknown profiles or unsupported actions remain unsupported. Entailed action inclusion never creates a new person's identity or delegated authority. Conflict strategy is distinct from rule applicability, policy validity, duty fulfillment, and execution permission.

theoretical positive test: A same-target permission to use and prohibition to print are conflicting under the declared print-includedIn-use relation. The public strategies yield permission precedence, prohibition precedence, or an invalid policy respectively. Permission precedence still leaves an unfulfilled duty outstanding.

theoretical adverse test: With no explicit strategy, a detected conflict invalidates the policy. Different inherited conflict values with conflicting rules cannot be resolved by picking the first record. Missing parent policies, ambiguous scope, unsupported vocabulary, or absent actor authentication cannot produce authorization.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for an interoperable, profile-bounded policy-composition layer. It makes precedence an explicit policy input instead of an engine accident.

public-data limit: The public standard does not grant private data-sharing rights. The bounded test uses RDFLib, NetworkX, and a small strategy reducer. OWL-RL, pySHACL, clingo, and Casbin composition was not executed.

required implementation and evidence: Archive the precise ontology and profile, qualify inherited/entailed rule expansion, test all conflict strategies and outstanding duties, and bind profile selection to a recorded authority decision. Compare full expansion with independent small policy tables.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: expanded-policy.json; asserted-and-derived-action-links.ttl; policy-conflicts.json; duty-state.json; authorization-envelope.json.

Libraries and primary references: S27 L02 L03 L10 L17 L67

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P293  version-bound record corrections -> staged JSON Patch and guarded commit -> atomic change with exact field lineage

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U05 U09 U10 U16 U17 U18
reuses: P126 validate-before-change pattern; P211 history; P244 stale-state fence; P245 schema migration; P262 canonical envelopes
new capability: python-json-patch and jsonpointer operations composed with Pydantic/jsonschema validation and a transactional version comparison
public basis: S28 Appendix A.1 adds an object member; A.2 inserts an array element. They supply exact public input/output examples. The case version, field permissions, database row, and failing multi-operation patch are authored fixtures.

```
current record version + authorized ordered patch + exact schema and path policy
-> validate patch structure, operation support, source identity, and field permissions (Pydantic; jsonschema; Casbin)
-> decode JSON Pointer escapes and bind array positions to the correct pre-operation state (jsonpointer.JsonPointer; resolve_pointer)
-> apply test and mutation operations to a private copy, preserving their order (jsonpatch.JsonPatch.apply with in_place=False)
-> validate the entire candidate and compute affected requirement/source paths (jsonschema; P212; typed dependency lookup)
-> commit only if the stored version still equals the expected version, within one transaction (sqlite3 or qualified provider conditional update; P244)
-> retain the old version, patch, candidate, commit receipt, and recheck triggers (prov; hashlib; JSON)
```

contract: An operation sequence must not leak partial changes after a failing test or schema check. Array insertion shifts later positions; pointer strings must not be treated as immutable business identities. A patch cannot edit an approval or policy field without separate permission. JSON numbers and booleans have distinct comparison semantics. Provider transaction behavior requires its own qualification.

theoretical positive test: The two public examples produce the specified object member and array insertion. A permitted address correction commits once against version 1. A second version-1 writer is stale. Escaped pointer tokens identify slash and tilde characters in keys correctly.

theoretical adverse test: A successful first mutation followed by a failed version test leaves the original unchanged. A forbidden path, malformed index, missing target, unsupported operation, or candidate failing its business schema aborts the patch. Boolean true cannot satisfy a numeric test for one.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for controlled client maintenance and post-review corrections with precise invalidation. Atomic update is an integration obligation in addition to patch syntax.

public-data limit: The reference test executes a deliberately restricted add/replace/remove/test adapter with jsonpointer and SQLite. The python-json-patch package, all RFC operations, concurrent processes, and remote commits were not exercised.

required implementation and evidence: Qualify the chosen full patch engine, numeric equality, root and nested paths, array behavior, whole-record schemas, permission scope, rollback, and concurrent version fences. Unsupported local reference operations remain explicitly unsupported.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: authorized-patch.json; staged-candidate.json; patch-commit-receipt.json; changed-field-lineage.json; correction-recheck-plan.json.

Libraries and primary references: S28 L02 L10 L17 L68

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P294  paginated source responses -> stable-snapshot and count reconciliation -> qualified evidence population

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U07 U08 U09 U13 U17 U18
reuses: P202 graph coverage; P210 source completeness; P211 snapshots; P242 duplicate identity; P266 API qualification
new capability: HTTPX transport-controlled pagination tests and strict page envelopes feeding a snapshot-qualified collection adapter
public basis: S20, RFC 7644 section 3.4.2.4, states that SCIM pagination is stateless and may return inconsistent results. Its startIndex, itemsPerPage, totalResults, and Resources fields provide the protocol shape. All returned IDs and the snapshot token in the reference test are authored.

```
authorized collection query + page contract + source snapshot guarantee or explicit absence
-> fix tenant, filters, sort keys, page size, source version, and acquisition bounds (Pydantic; canonical query envelope)
-> retrieve each page through a bounded adapter, preserving request/response provenance (httpx.Client; response JSON; retry policy from P295)
-> validate page indices, counts, record IDs, duplicate payloads, and continuation progress (Pydantic; pandas joins; P210)
-> reconcile changing totals, missing pages, repeated cursors, and version tokens (typed collection reducer; HTTPX MockTransport tests)
-> require a qualified provider snapshot or equivalent export guarantee before asserting snapshot completeness (explicit assurance gate; P199)
-> seal accepted records together with acquisition limits and unresolved coverage (prov; hashlib; JSON)
```

contract: Matching row counts cannot establish a point-in-time population when records can change between pages. A repeated total or client-created token does not supply a provider snapshot. A short page is interpreted under the provider contract. A missing or forbidden page remains missing, rather than an empty population. Retries preserve all conflicting observations.

theoretical positive test: Under an explicitly authored provider snapshot guarantee, two pages starting at 1 and 3 contain a, b, and c, with total three and one matching snapshot token. They form a complete collection under that declared contract. Removing the guarantee yields coverage_unproven even with the same rows.

theoretical adverse test: Missing the last page gives incomplete coverage. A duplicate ID, altered total, nonadvancing continuation, or wrong page index is inconsistent. A changed snapshot token blocks complete-snapshot status. Two records can change between pages while the total stays constant; total equality alone must not pass.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for defensible acquisition and completeness accounting. The distinction directly protects ownership coverage, review populations, and conformance denominators.

public-data limit: The test executes HTTPX MockTransport and strict Pydantic page parsing with no network traffic. No live SCIM provider, full public registry, or provider snapshot guarantee is qualified.

required implementation and evidence: Specify provider continuation semantics, enforce bounded acquisition, archive every page and exact query, test mutations between pages, and obtain evidence for any claimed snapshot guarantee. Preserve coverage limits downstream.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: source-page-manifest.json; reconciled-source-population.json; pagination-conflicts.json; snapshot-coverage.json.

Libraries and primary references: S20 L06 L17 L69

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P295  provider rate limits and transient failures -> bounded retry schedule -> evidence acquisition without false absence

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U05 U10 U11 U16 U17 U18
reuses: P199 unknown gates; P218 time horizons; P241 durable timers; P242 retry reconciliation; P294 collection coverage
new capability: Tenacity retry/stop/wait policies with HTTPX response classification and explicit provider Retry-After parsing
public basis: S29 supplies Retry-After as seconds or an HTTP date, with examples 120 and Fri, 31 Dec 1999 23:59:59 GMT. S30 supplies the 429 response. Test response sequences and elapsed budgets are authored.

```
approved evidence request + method/effect contract + attempt and elapsed budgets
-> classify transport failure, rate limit, transient unavailability, authentication failure, and source absence separately (HTTPX; typed status adapter)
-> parse supported server waits without shortening them and retain clock uncertainty (email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime; datetime; explicit rounding)
-> combine the server lower bound with reviewed backoff and total-budget limits (tenacity.Retrying; retry and stop policies; custom wait adapter)
-> persist a deferred request when waiting would exceed the present execution budget (Temporal timer/state; P241)
-> reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying any side-effecting operation (P242; provider receipts)
-> emit retrieved bytes, deferred acquisition, or a terminal error with coverage status (prov; P294)
```

contract: Rate limits and failed authentication must never become evidence that a document or person does not exist. The qualified read-only profile can retry declared retrieval methods; side-effecting methods need separate idempotency and reconciliation evidence. Retry limits are enforced across restarts. Circuit breaking is an additional proposed runtime policy, not a property of a successful request.

theoretical positive test: The public value 120 means a 120-second wait. At the authored 23:57:59 UTC clock, the public HTTP-date example also yields 120. An authored 503 followed by 200 succeeds after the modeled wait, while received bytes still require content validation.

theoretical adverse test: A 120-second wait with only 100 seconds left defers the request. Authentication failure ends the local retry path. A non-idempotent POST with an uncertain outcome is not retried by the read-only adapter. Invalid waits, infinite zero-delay retries, or lost cumulative budgets cannot silently pass.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for bounded, auditable source acquisition. It improves acquisition reliability without turning availability into truth or permission.

public-data limit: The reference uses a finite response reducer and clock arithmetic. It makes no network requests or real sleeps. Tenacity, distributed budgets, durable timers, and live provider behavior were not executed.

required implementation and evidence: Pin the response taxonomy, server-wait policy, monotonic time mapping, exception classes, backoff, circuit/reset rules, and persistent budget state. Test restarts and uncertain remote outcomes in an authorized integration environment.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: acquisition-attempt-ledger.json; deferred-source-requests.json; retry-budget-state.json; unavailable-source-evidence.json.

Libraries and primary references: S29 S30 L17 L31 L69 L70

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P296  copied and independently attributed evidence -> origin-aware support groups -> corroboration without counting mirrors as new sources

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U01 U05 U07 U08 U16 U17
reuses: P17 integrity hashes; P201 linkage limits; P213 sufficient supports; P247 attribution checks; P284 reversible identity
new capability: PROV derivation/attribution records composed with typed NetworkX origin traversal and pySHACL lineage-completeness checks
public basis: L06/L71 provides a public provenance data model. The original record, two mirrors, extra source, and attribution attestations below are authored. A wasDerivedFrom edge records a relationship; it does not prove that the relationship is true.

```
evidence records + declared derivation links + issuer/source attestations + corroboration policy
-> distinguish document identity, byte identity, underlying observation, and publisher identity (Pydantic; hashlib; P201)
-> retain asserted derivation and attribution with versioned source references (RDFLib PROV vocabulary; prov.ProvDocument)
-> validate endpoints, provenance gaps, and the declared acyclic transformation subset (pySHACL; NetworkX)
-> trace each evidence item to known origin groups without inventing absent links (networkx.descendants; typed origin adapter)
-> evaluate explicit sufficient-support groups after collapsing documented mirrors (clingo; P213; independent set oracle)
-> return support, contradicted support, shared-origin explanations, and unresolved origin assumptions (prov; Jinja2)
```

contract: Three URLs may reproduce one observation. Different URLs, file hashes, or company names do not establish independent evidence. Known distinct origin groups also do not establish statistical independence or truth. The acceptance rule must identify what kind of independence it requires and how that property is evidenced. Ambiguous source linkage stays unresolved.

theoretical positive test: An original record and two documented mirrors produce one known origin group. A separately attested source record produces a second group while retaining all four document identities. Withdrawing the original invalidates its dependent support under the relevant source policy.

theoretical adverse test: A scraper cache cannot count as an additional corroborating source merely because it has another filename. An unknown derivation root cannot become a confirmed independent origin. A cyclic transformation graph fails this adapter's declared DAG contract. A contradictory direct record stays visible after deduplication.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for source-sensitive evidence evaluation. It complements P213, which tracks sufficient support, by preventing copied support from being mistaken for new observations.

public-data limit: The bounded test executes RDFLib and NetworkX on authored provenance. It does not authenticate publishers, establish source independence, or measure evidence reliability. The prov package, SHACL layer, and policy engine remain unexecuted.

required implementation and evidence: Define origin granularity and attestations, qualify derivation adapters, test missing/cyclic links and retractions, and require independent review of any substantive corroboration rule. Keep observation identity separate from document identity.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: evidence-origin-groups.json; shared-origin-support.json; provenance-gaps.json; corroboration-decisions.json.

Libraries and primary references: L02 L03 L06 L17 L71

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.


## P297  derived query fields and selection predicates -> typed column lineage -> complete change-impact candidates for reports and gates

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U06 U13 U14 U15 U17 U18
reuses: P95 schemas; P212 change impact; P285 controlled query plans; P290 dependency-key completeness
new capability: SQLGlot column-lineage analysis plus explicit predicate, join, ordering, and authorization dependencies
public basis: L72 documents SQLGlot's lineage interface with explicit schemas, source queries, and dialects. The source table, monetary-looking integers, region filter, SQL, and dependency graph are authored mechanics fixtures with no financial interpretation.

```
approved SQL expression + resolved schema + source-query versions + authorization context

```

contract: A field can affect whether a row exists without appearing in its output expression. Value-only lineage is insufficient for report completeness or cached authorization. SELECT star requires the exact schema version. Dynamic SQL, opaque functions, unresolved identifiers, and unsupported dialect features block a complete-lineage claim. Conservative extra dependencies are recorded separately from proven necessary dependencies.

theoretical positive test: A query computes gross minus credit as net for region A. The authored row initially returns net 80. Changing only region to B removes the row while its arithmetic value stays 80. Region must therefore invalidate the reported result even though it is absent from the arithmetic expression.

theoretical adverse test: A projection-only map misses that change. An untracked join filter, renamed column, changed authorization predicate, or changed ordering before LIMIT must prevent reuse of a claimed complete dependency key. Parsing an unresolved query cannot certify lineage.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for finer-grained impact analysis and guarded recomputation. It extends case-level provenance to data-transformation semantics.

public-data limit: The local reference executes an authored dependency graph and actual SQLite queries. SQLGlot extraction, arbitrary SQL, real warehouse schemas, and optimizer equivalence were not tested.

required implementation and evidence: Qualify the supported SQL subset, pair column lineage with predicate visitors, include schema and access-policy versions, and compare dependency-triggered reruns with complete recomputation across controlled mutations.

## P298  operational aggregates and protected-unit limits -> reviewed privacy mechanism and budget reservation -> controlled statistical release

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U06 U13 U14 U16 U17
reuses: P231 interval measures; P240 contributor conservation; P242 idempotent ledger; P264 nonleaking views; P279 declared loss tradeoffs
new capability: OpenDP measurement/composition objects with explicit contribution bounding and a transactional privacy-budget ledger
public basis: L73 defines a supported composition operation and its domain/metric compatibility requirements. The contribution bound, epsilon values, records, and reservation IDs below are authored mathematical fixtures. No private dataset or noisy statistical release is used.

```
approved statistical question + protected-unit definition + contribution limits + release policy
-> separate persons/cases from events and bind the adjacency relation and cohort (Pydantic; exact contributor identities; P231)
-> apply a reviewed contribution-bounding transformation with a known stability contract (OpenDP transformation API; independent bounded-neighbor tests)
-> construct a supported measurement and inspect its privacy map against the chosen input distance (OpenDP measurement API; Measurement.map/check)
-> compose compatible measurements under the approved accounting model (opendp.combinators.make_basic_composition or separately qualified adaptive composition)
-> reserve the full privacy cost atomically before any new release can escape (sqlite3 transaction; immutable release IDs; P242)
```

contract: Event-level limits do not automatically establish person-level privacy. Protected-unit linkage, contribution bounds, adjacency, domains, metrics, randomness, epsilon, and delta must be reviewed together. Basic sequential accounting sums compatible costs. Parallel composition requires demonstrated disjoint protected units. Repeated fresh noise draws are new releases. A private seed or raw count must not leak through test logs or metadata. A budget ledger alone proves no privacy guarantee.

theoretical positive test: Under an authored person-level model, events 7, 8, and 9 for one person are aggregated and clipped to ten; another person contributes four. Removing the first person's contribution changes the bounded sum by ten. Two approved pure-DP costs of 2/5 and 3/5 exhaust a budget of one.

theoretical adverse test: Clipping each event separately still allows the first person to contribute 24. A further release costing 1/1000 is rejected after the two reservations. A changed immutable reservation, negative budget, changed cohort, incompatible metric, or unaccounted fresh draw cannot pass.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for an optional statistical-release layer after full privacy and utility qualification. This can support program measurement while keeping case-level execution evidence under separate access controls.

public-data limit: Only exact contribution and budget accounting runs locally. OpenDP mechanisms, secure randomness, empirical utility, adaptive composition, and privacy guarantees were not executed or established. This proof makes no legal anonymization determination.

Validate utility separately from privacy. Preserve failed reservations and consumed budgets honestly.

## P299  locale-tagged numeric evidence -> exact parsing and semantic typing -> source-preserving international input

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U01 U02 U05 U07 U17 U18
reuses: P191 supported syntax; P195 source-offset preservation; P282 units and meaning; P288 annotation disagreement
new capability: Babel locale/numbering-system parsing composed with Decimal, Lark field grammars, Pydantic types, and explicit strictness policy
public basis: L74 publishes decimal examples for English, German, Russian, and Egyptian Arabic conventions. Their expected numeric values are used as public projections. The ambiguous 1,234 comparison, schema, and rejection variants are authored tests.

```
source span + explicit locale/numbering system + field type + approved parsing profile
-> retain original characters and normalization offsets without guessing locale from a person's identity (P195; Pydantic)
-> restrict the admitted lexical form and field semantics (Lark; explicit amount/count/percentage grammar)
-> parse using the declared locale, numbering system, and strictness (babel.numbers.parse_decimal)
-> reject nonfinite values and enforce currency/unit/range/precision independently (decimal.Decimal; Pydantic; P282)
-> format only for display with an explicit quantization policy, then verify the intended roundtrip (Babel format_decimal; Decimal comparison)
-> return exact value, source span, parser profile, and unresolved-locale or unsupported-form state (prov; JSON)
```

contract: Locale parsing establishes a numeric interpretation under a chosen convention. It does not validate a translation, issuer, currency, field meaning, or document authenticity. The same characters can have different values under different locales. The machine's default locale is never a silent input. Lenient and strict parsing are separate supported modes; changing one is a profile change.

theoretical positive test: The documented strings 1,099.98, 1.099,98, 12 345,123, and the documented Arabic-separator example yield their stated Decimal values under the published default parsing mode. The authored value 1,234 means 1234 with en_US and 1.234 with de_DE. Without a locale, the adapter returns unresolved.

theoretical adverse test: A German-formatted number under strict en_US parsing is rejected. NaN cannot become a valid amount. In the tested Babel environment, the published Russian example with an ordinary space is accepted leniently and rejected strictly; a separately labeled nonbreaking-space variant passes strict parsing. Rounding a high-precision source for display cannot overwrite the exact stored value.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for deterministic international form and evidence ingestion. The strict/lenient distinction is an observed boundary that must be part of the adapter contract.

public-data limit: Babel numeric functions actually run on the cited examples. General multilingual document extraction, translation fidelity, date interpretation, and private form coverage remain untested. The example projection is not a complete locale conformance suite.

required implementation and evidence: Pin Babel and its locale data; version the admitted formats and strictness; qualify missing locale, alternative spaces, numbering systems, nonfinite inputs, excess precision, and exact/display roundtrips. Keep unsupported natural-language amounts outside the accepted grammar.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: locale-bound-values.json; parsing-profile-register.json; unsupported-numeric-spans.json; exact-display-roundtrip.json.

## P300  interrupted source downloads -> version-bound byte-range reconciliation -> complete evidence bytes or explicit incomplete acquisition

**theoretical requirement; full chain not executed**

use cases: U05 U08 U13 U17 U18
reuses: P17 integrity; P210 coverage conservation; P247 trusted attribution; P265 sealed registry; P269 checkpoint restore; P294 acquisition coverage
new capability: fsspec storage adapters with HTTPX raw response handling, explicit Content-Range validation, and whole-object integrity gates
public basis: S29 section 14.4 supplies the public headers bytes 42-1233/1234 and bytes 42-1233/*. The ten-byte payload, strong ETag, chunks, interruption, and corrupted variants below are authored.

```
permitted source object + expected version/length/hash contract + retained partial chunks
-> bind all requests to one selected representation and byte-coordinate convention (HTTPX headers; explicit content-encoding policy)
-> validate 206 status, Content-Range, payload length, total length, and matching strong version validators (typed range parser; Pydantic)
-> reconcile chunk coverage, duplicates, and conflicting overlap without concatenating by arrival order (interval accounting; hashlib; P210)
-> stage only validated bytes through the selected storage backend (fsspec filesystem/cat_file/pipe_file; backend-specific adapter)
-> require complete byte coverage and an independently trusted whole-object digest before final publication (hashlib.sha256; explicit integrity gate)
-> publish atomically only on a backend whose commit behavior is qualified, retaining source and acquisition evidence (local os.replace or qualified remote commit; prov)
```

contract: Public byte-range endpoints are inclusive; internal half-open intervals need an explicit conversion. Encoded and decoded byte offsets must not be mixed. A 200 response to a range request requires a separately validated full-representation path. Unknown total length, inconsistent versions, or conflicting bytes block this profile's completion claim. An ETag is a representation validator, not a cryptographic identity assertion. A hash is trusted only through an independent expected-value chain.

theoretical positive test: The public known-length header maps to internal interval [42,1234), length 1192, total 1234. Two authored chunks [0,4) and [4,10) reconstruct exactly 0123456789 in either arrival order. fsspec's memory backend reads back the same ten bytes after verification.

theoretical adverse test: A missing chunk, changed ETag, invalid range, wrong length, conflicting overlap, or wrong full-object hash prevents completion. The public unknown-total header remains unresolved for complete coverage. A full 200 response must not be appended to an existing partial file. A weak version validator is outside this selected profile.

assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for resumable evidence acquisition and archive recovery. This proves a separate byte-integrity boundary before semantic parsing or evidence use.

public-data limit: The bounded test executes header parsing, HTTPX response objects, hashes, and fsspec memory storage with no network traffic. Live server behavior, HTTP backend range reads, large files, disk crashes, durable atomic publication, and source authenticity remain unqualified.

required implementation and evidence: Define raw versus decoded byte handling, backend commit guarantees, maximum object/chunk sizes, empty-object behavior, resume manifests, trusted digest acquisition, and source permission. Test complete/missing/mixed-version ranges and forced interruption before promotion.

planned outputs, not created as full-chain outputs: source-chunk-manifest.json; chunk-conflicts.json; complete-object-receipt.json; acquisition-coverage.json; resumable-source-provenance.json.

Libraries and primary references: S29 L17 L69 L75

execution requirement: Fixed function handoffs; zero LLM reasoning intervention between functions or chains.

### Embedded reference program for P291-P300

```python
"""Offline bounded reference checks for P291-P300. These do not execute full chains.
Public projections: ODRL conflict terms; RFC 6902 A.1/A.2; RFC 9110 header
examples; Babel parse_decimal examples. All other records are authored fixtures.
Run with Python and the versions recorded in the emitted report. No network calls.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import copy
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from fractions import Fraction
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import itertools
import math
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
import traceback
import babel.numbers as bn
import fsspec
import httpx
from jsonpointer import JsonPointer, resolve_pointer
import networkx as nx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError
from rdflib import Graph, Namespace
from sympy import Matrix, Rational, eye

CASES = []
ASSERTIONS = 0

def check(value, message):
    global ASSERTIONS
    ASSERTIONS += 1
    if not value:
        raise AssertionError(message)

def eq(actual, expected):
    check(actual == expected, f'{actual!r} != {expected!r}')

def rejects(exc, function):
    try:
        function()
    except exc:
        check(True, 'expected rejection')
    else:
        check(False, f'Expected {exc.__name__}')

def case(proof):
    def register(function):
        CASES.append((proof, function))
        return function
    return register

def canon(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False,
                      separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8')

def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

@case(291)
def cyclic_ownership():
    # C[owner_company, issuer_company]; x = d + C.T*x.
    c = Matrix([[0, Rational(1, 2)], [Rational(1, 4), 0]])
    g = nx.DiGraph([('A', 'B'), ('B', 'A')])
    eq(list(nx.strongly_connected_components(g)), [{'A', 'B'}])
    a = eye(2) - c.T
    d1 = Matrix([Rational(1, 2), 0])
    x1 = a.LUsolve(d1)
    eq(list(x1), [Rational(4, 7), Rational(2, 7)])
    eq(a*x1, d1)
    # Independent two-equation elimination with Fraction.
    xa = Fraction(1, 2)/(1-Fraction(1, 2)*Fraction(1, 4))
    xb = xa*Fraction(1, 2)
    eq([str(v) for v in x1], [str(xa), str(xb)])
    d2 = Matrix([Rational(1, 4), Rational(1, 2)])
    x2 = a.LUsolve(d2)
    eq(list(x1+x2), [1, 1])
    singular = eye(2)-Matrix([[0, 1], [1, 0]]).T
    eq(singular.det(), 0)
    eq(singular.rank(), 1)
    check(max(sum(c[i,j] for i in range(2)) for j in range(2)) < 1,
          'conservative convergence certificate absent')
    return {'authored_person1_economic_shares': [str(x) for x in x1],
            'all_external_shares_conserve_each_issuer': True,
            'closed_mutual_100_percent_block': 'unresolved_singular',
            'beneficial_owner_or_control_determination': False}

@case(292)
def odrl_conflicts():
    od = Namespace('http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/')
    g = Graph()
    g.add((od['print'], od['includedIn'], od['use']))
    edges = nx.DiGraph((str(s), str(o)) for s,_,o in g)
    inherited = str(od['use']) in nx.descendants(edges, str(od['print']))
    check(inherited, 'encompassing action not resolved')
    def resolve(conflict_terms, duties_satisfied=True, known_vocabulary=True):
        if not known_vocabulary:
            return 'unsupported'
        terms = set(conflict_terms) or {'invalid'}
        if len(terms) != 1 or 'invalid' in terms:
            return 'invalid_policy'
        term = next(iter(terms))
        if term == 'prohibit':
            return 'prohibited'
        if term == 'perm':
            return 'permitted_under_profile' if duties_satisfied else 'duty_outstanding'
        return 'unsupported'
    eq(resolve([]), 'invalid_policy')
    eq(resolve(['perm']), 'permitted_under_profile')
    eq(resolve(['prohibit']), 'prohibited')
    eq(resolve(['perm', 'prohibit']), 'invalid_policy')
    eq(resolve(['perm'], False), 'duty_outstanding')
    eq(resolve(['perm'], known_vocabulary=False), 'unsupported')
    eq(resolve(['unknown-term']), 'unsupported')
    return {'public_profile': 'ODRL 2.2 section 2.10',
            'explicit_conflict_outcomes_checked': 7,
            'owlrl_pyshacl_clingo_executed': False,
            'organizational_authority_established': False}

def json_equal(a, b):
    # RFC JSON numeric equality excludes booleans. Nonfinite numbers rejected upstream.
    numeric = lambda x: type(x) in (int, float)
    if numeric(a) and numeric(b):
        return a == b
    if type(a) is not type(b):
        return False
    if isinstance(a, dict):
        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(json_equal(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
    if isinstance(a, list):
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(json_equal(x,y) for x,y in zip(a,b))
    return a == b

def staged_patch(document, operations, allowed_paths=None):
    """Deliberately restricted subset: add, replace, remove, test; nonroot paths.
    Not a complete RFC 6902 implementation. Mutations occur only in a private copy.
    """
    canon(document); canon(operations)
    candidate = copy.deepcopy(document)
    for op in operations:
        kind, path = op['op'], op['path']
        if kind not in {'add','replace','remove','test'} or not path.startswith('/'):
            raise ValueError('unsupported operation or root path')
        if allowed_paths is not None and path not in allowed_paths:
            raise ValueError('unauthorized exact path')
        parts = JsonPointer(path).parts
        parent = candidate
        for part in parts[:-1]:
            parent = parent[int(part)] if isinstance(parent, list) else parent[part]
        key = parts[-1]
        if kind == 'test':
            if not json_equal(resolve_pointer(candidate, path), op['value']):
                raise ValueError('failed test')
            continue
        if isinstance(parent, list):
            if key == '-' and kind == 'add':
                index = len(parent)
            elif re.fullmatch(r'0|[1-9][0-9]*', key):
                index = int(key)
            else:
                raise ValueError('invalid array index')
            if kind == 'add':
                if index > len(parent): raise ValueError('index beyond array')
                parent.insert(index, copy.deepcopy(op['value']))
            else:
                if index >= len(parent): raise ValueError('missing target')
                if kind == 'replace': parent[index] = copy.deepcopy(op['value'])
                else: parent.pop(index)
        elif isinstance(parent, dict):
            if kind in {'replace','remove'} and key not in parent:
                raise ValueError('missing target')
            if kind == 'remove': del parent[key]
            else: parent[key] = copy.deepcopy(op['value'])
        else:
            raise ValueError('target parent is not a container')
    return candidate

@case(293)
def atomic_json_corrections():
    # RFC 6902 Appendix A.1 and A.2, manually projected from the public RFC.
    eq(staged_patch({'foo':'bar'}, [{'op':'add','path':'/baz','value':'qux'}]),
       {'foo':'bar','baz':'qux'})
    eq(staged_patch({'foo':['bar','baz']}, [{'op':'add','path':'/foo/1','value':'qux'}]),
       {'foo':['bar','qux','baz']})
    original = {'version':1,'address':'old'}
    before = canon(original)
    rejects(ValueError, lambda: staged_patch(original,[
        {'op':'replace','path':'/address','value':'new'},
        {'op':'test','path':'/version','value':2}]))
    eq(canon(original), before)
    rejects(ValueError, lambda: staged_patch(original,
        [{'op':'replace','path':'/version','value':2}], {'/address'}))
    eq(staged_patch({'a/b':1,'m~n':2}, [
        {'op':'test','path':'/a~1b','value':1},
        {'op':'test','path':'/m~0n','value':2}]), {'a/b':1,'m~n':2})
    rejects(ValueError, lambda: staged_patch({'v':True},
        [{'op':'test','path':'/v','value':1}]))
    eq(staged_patch({'v':1}, [{'op':'test','path':'/v','value':1.0}]), {'v':1})
    rejects(ValueError, lambda: staged_patch(original,
        [{'op':'move','path':'/address','from':'/version'}]))
    with sqlite3.connect(':memory:') as db:
        db.execute('CREATE TABLE c(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, version INT, body TEXT)')
        db.execute('INSERT INTO c VALUES(?,?,?)', ('c1',1,before.decode()))
        updated = staged_patch(original,[{'op':'replace','path':'/address','value':'new'}])
        eq(db.execute('UPDATE c SET body=?,version=2 WHERE id=? AND version=1',
                      (canon(updated).decode(),'c1')).rowcount, 1)
        eq(db.execute('UPDATE c SET body=? WHERE id=? AND version=1',
                      ('stale','c1')).rowcount, 0)
    return {'public_patch_examples_checked': ['A.1','A.2'],
            'staged_failure_preserves_original': True,
            'stale_write_rejected': True, 'python_json_patch_executed': False}

class Page(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, extra='forbid')
    startIndex: int = Field(ge=1)
    itemsPerPage: int = Field(ge=0)
    totalResults: int = Field(ge=0)
    Resources: list[dict[str,str]]
    snapshot: str | None = None

def reconcile_pages(raw_pages, snapshot_guaranteed=False):
    pages = [Page.model_validate(p) for p in raw_pages]
    if not pages: return 'incomplete', []
    total = pages[0].totalResults
    seen = set(); rows = []; next_start = 1
    snapshots = {p.snapshot for p in pages}
    for p in pages:
        if p.startIndex != next_start or p.itemsPerPage != len(p.Resources):
            return 'inconsistent', rows
        if p.totalResults != total: return 'inconsistent', rows
        for r in p.Resources:
            if r['id'] in seen: return 'inconsistent', rows
            seen.add(r['id']); rows.append(r)
        next_start += len(p.Resources)
    if len(rows) != total: return 'incomplete', rows
    if not snapshot_guaranteed or None in snapshots or len(snapshots) != 1:
        return 'coverage_unproven', rows
    return 'complete_under_declared_snapshot_contract', rows

@case(294)
def paginated_collection():
    pages=[{'startIndex':1,'itemsPerPage':2,'totalResults':3,
            'Resources':[{'id':'a'},{'id':'b'}],'snapshot':'s1'},
           {'startIndex':3,'itemsPerPage':1,'totalResults':3,
            'Resources':[{'id':'c'}],'snapshot':'s1'}]
    requests=[]
    def handler(request):
        requests.append(str(request.url))
        start=int(request.url.params['startIndex'])
        return httpx.Response(200,json=pages[0 if start==1 else 1])
    with httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)) as client:
        retrieved=[client.get('https://example.invalid/resources',
                   params={'startIndex':s}).json() for s in (1,3)]
    eq(len(requests),2)
    eq(reconcile_pages(retrieved,True)[0],'complete_under_declared_snapshot_contract')
    eq(reconcile_pages(retrieved,False)[0],'coverage_unproven')
    eq(reconcile_pages(retrieved[:1],True)[0],'incomplete')
    duplicate=copy.deepcopy(retrieved);duplicate[1]['Resources'][0]['id']='b'
    eq(reconcile_pages(duplicate,True)[0],'inconsistent')
    changed=copy.deepcopy(retrieved);changed[1]['totalResults']=4
    eq(reconcile_pages(changed,True)[0],'inconsistent')
    changed=copy.deepcopy(retrieved);changed[1]['snapshot']='s2'
    eq(reconcile_pages(changed,True)[0],'coverage_unproven')
    rejects(ValidationError,lambda:Page.model_validate(pages[0]|{'startIndex':True}))
    return {'mocked_pages':2,'network_requests':0,'snapshot_token':'authored extension, not SCIM guarantee',
            'bare_SCIM_full_snapshot_qualified':False}

def retry_delay(value, now):
    if re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+', value): return int(value)
    try:
        target=parsedate_to_datetime(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError('invalid Retry-After')
    if target.tzinfo is None: raise ValueError('timezone required')
    return max(0, math.ceil((target-now).total_seconds()))

@case(295)
def governed_retry_budget():
    now=datetime(1999,12,31,23,57,59,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    eq(retry_delay('120',now),120)
    eq(retry_delay('Fri, 31 Dec 1999 23:59:59 GMT',now),120)
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:retry_delay('-1',now))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:retry_delay('later',now))
    def simulate(statuses, max_elapsed=200, method='GET'):
        if method!='GET': return {'outcome':'unsafe_to_retry','attempts':0,'elapsed':0}
        elapsed=0; attempts=0
        for status,header in statuses[:3]:
            attempts+=1
            if status==200: return {'outcome':'bytes_received_unvalidated','attempts':attempts,'elapsed':elapsed}
            if status not in {429,503}: return {'outcome':'terminal_error','attempts':attempts,'elapsed':elapsed}
            delay=retry_delay(header,now)
            if elapsed+delay>max_elapsed: return {'outcome':'deferred','attempts':attempts,'elapsed':elapsed}
            elapsed+=delay
        return {'outcome':'retry_budget_exhausted','attempts':attempts,'elapsed':elapsed}
    eq(simulate([(503,'120'),(200,'')]),
       {'outcome':'bytes_received_unvalidated','attempts':2,'elapsed':120})
    eq(simulate([(429,'120')],100)['outcome'],'deferred')
    eq(simulate([(401,''),(200,'')])['attempts'],1)
    eq(simulate([(503,'120')],method='POST')['outcome'],'unsafe_to_retry')
    eq(simulate([(503,'0')]*8)['attempts'],3)
    return {'public_header_examples_checked':2,'actual_sleep_seconds':0,
            'network_requests':0,'tenacity_executed':False}

@case(296)
def origin_aware_corroboration():
    prov=Namespace('http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#'); ex=Namespace('urn:p296:')
    rdf=Graph()
    for child,parent in [('mirror1','original'),('mirror2','original')]:
        rdf.add((ex[child],prov['wasDerivedFrom'],ex[parent]))
    # Derived -> source orientation, not inferred from matching names or bytes.
    g=nx.DiGraph((str(s),str(o)) for s,_,o in rdf)
    g.add_node(str(ex['independent_record']))
    attested_roots={str(ex['original']):'issuer_record_1',
                    str(ex['independent_record']):'issuer_record_2'}
    def roots_for(evidence):
        origins=set();unresolved=[]
        for item in evidence:
            if item not in g:
                unresolved.append(item);continue
            nodes=nx.descendants(g,item)|{item}
            roots={n for n in nodes if g.out_degree(n)==0}
            for root in roots:
                if root in attested_roots: origins.add(attested_roots[root])
                else: unresolved.append(root)
        return origins,unresolved
    ids=[str(ex[x]) for x in ('original','mirror1','mirror2')]
    eq(roots_for(ids),({'issuer_record_1'},[]))
    eq(roots_for(ids+[str(ex['independent_record'])])[0],
       {'issuer_record_1','issuer_record_2'})
    eq(len(roots_for(ids+[str(ex['unknown'])])[1]),1)
    g.add_edge(str(ex['original']),str(ex['mirror1']))
    check(not nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(g),'cyclic derivation escaped the declared DAG gate')
    return {'three_documents_known_origin_groups':1,
            'additional_attested_record_origin_groups':2,
            'statistical_independence_or_truth_proven':False,'prov_package_executed':False}

@case(297)
def field_and_predicate_lineage():
    # Explicit fixture graph. This does not pretend to extract SQLGlot lineage.
    g=nx.DiGraph()
    for source in ('gross','credit'):g.add_edge(source,'net_value',kind='value')
    g.add_edge('region','row_membership',kind='predicate')
    g.add_edge('row_membership','reported_net',kind='membership')
    g.add_edge('net_value','reported_net',kind='value')
    eq(nx.descendants(g,'region'),{'row_membership','reported_net'})
    eq(nx.descendants(g,'gross'),{'net_value','reported_net'})
    with sqlite3.connect(':memory:') as db:
        db.execute('CREATE TABLE c(id TEXT, gross INT, credit INT, region TEXT)')
        db.execute('INSERT INTO c VALUES(?,?,?,?)',('c1',100,20,'A'))
        q='SELECT id, gross-credit AS net FROM c WHERE region=?'
        eq(db.execute(q,('A',)).fetchall(),[('c1',80)])
        db.execute('UPDATE c SET region=? WHERE id=?',('B','c1'))
        eq(db.execute(q,('A',)).fetchall(),[])
        eq(db.execute('SELECT gross-credit FROM c').fetchone()[0],80)
    expected={'gross','credit','region'}
    value_only={'gross','credit'}
    eq(expected-value_only,{'region'})
    return {'unchanged_value_but_changed_result_membership':True,
            'SQLGlot_lineage_executed':False,'arbitrary_SQL_lineage_qualified':False}

@case(298)
def contribution_bounds_and_privacy_budget():
    # Pure accounting, no DP mechanism or private dataset is executed.
    records={'person1':[7,8,9],'person2':[4]}
    bounded={k:min(10,max(0,sum(v))) for k,v in records.items()}
    eq(bounded,{'person1':10,'person2':4})
    eq(sum(bounded.values())-bounded['person2'],10)
    check(sum(min(10,x) for x in records['person1'])>10,
          'event-level clipping accidentally meets person-level bound')
    eps=[Fraction(2,5),Fraction(3,5)]
    eq(sum(eps),Fraction(1))
    check(sum(eps)+Fraction(1,1000)>Fraction(1),'extra release escaped budget')
    reserved={}
    def reserve(release,amount):
        if not isinstance(amount,Fraction) or amount<=0: raise ValueError('positive exact budget required')
        if release in reserved:
            if reserved[release]!=amount: raise ValueError('changed immutable reservation')
            return 'existing'
        if sum(reserved.values())+amount>1:return 'denied'
        reserved[release]=amount;return 'reserved'
    eq(reserve('r1',eps[0]),'reserved');eq(reserve('r1',eps[0]),'existing')
    eq(reserve('r2',eps[1]),'reserved')
    eq(reserve('r3',Fraction(1,1000)),'denied')
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:reserve('r1',Fraction(1,5)))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:reserve('bad',Fraction(-1)))
    return {'person_contribution_bound':10,'basic_epsilon_total':'1',
            'privacy_accounting_only':True,'OpenDP_executed':False,
            'private_releases':0,'privacy_guarantee_established':False}

@case(299)
def explicit_locale_numbers():
    # The following four strings and expected values are from Babel documentation.
    examples=[('1,099.98','en_US','latn','1099.98'),
              ('1.099,98','de','latn','1099.98'),
              ('12 345,123','ru','latn','12345.123'),
              ('1\u066c099\u066b98','ar_EG','default','1099.98')]
    observed=[]
    for value,locale,system,expected in examples:
        result=bn.parse_decimal(value,locale=locale,numbering_system=system,strict=False)
        eq(result,Decimal(expected));observed.append(str(result))
    # Published examples use the default lenient mode; test strict mode separately.
    rejects(bn.NumberFormatError, lambda: bn.parse_decimal('12 345,123',locale='ru',strict=True))
    eq(bn.parse_decimal('12\u00a0345,123',locale='ru',strict=True),Decimal('12345.123'))
    eq(bn.parse_decimal('1,234',locale='en_US',strict=True),Decimal('1234'))
    eq(bn.parse_decimal('1,234',locale='de_DE',strict=True),Decimal('1.234'))
    def convert(value,locale):
        if locale is None: return 'unresolved_locale'
        parsed=bn.parse_decimal(value,locale=locale,strict=True)
        if not parsed.is_finite(): raise ValueError('nonfinite input')
        return parsed
    eq(convert('1,234',None),'unresolved_locale')
    rejects(bn.NumberFormatError,lambda:convert('1.099,98','en_US'))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:convert('NaN','en_US'))
    exact=Decimal('1099.9876')
    rendered=bn.format_decimal(exact,locale='en_US',decimal_quantization=False)
    eq(bn.parse_decimal(rendered,locale='en_US',strict=True),exact)
    return {'public_examples_checked':4,'canonical_decimals':observed,'strict_mode_ascii_space_rejected':True,
            'ambiguous_separator_without_locale':'unresolved',
            'linguistic_or_legal_translation_validated':False}

def content_range(value):
    m=re.fullmatch(r'bytes ([0-9]+)-([0-9]+)/(\*|[0-9]+)',value)
    if not m:raise ValueError('unsupported Content-Range form')
    start,end=map(int,m.group(1,2));total=None if m[3]=='*' else int(m[3])
    if end<start or (total is not None and end>=total):raise ValueError('invalid range')
    return start,end+1,total

def assemble(parts,expected_etag,expected_hash):
    if not re.fullmatch(r'"[\x21\x23-\x7e\x80-\xff]*"', expected_etag):
        raise ValueError('strong version validator required by local contract')
    total=None; values={}
    for response in parts:
        if response.status_code!=206:raise ValueError('full response requires separate restart path')
        if response.headers.get('etag')!=expected_etag:raise ValueError('representation changed')
        a,b,n=content_range(response.headers['content-range'])
        if n is None:raise ValueError('unknown total')
        if total is not None and total!=n:raise ValueError('inconsistent total')
        total=n
        if len(response.content)!=b-a:raise ValueError('payload length mismatch')
        for i,v in enumerate(response.content,a):
            if i in values and values[i]!=v:raise ValueError('conflicting overlap')
            values[i]=v
    if total is None or len(values)!=total:raise ValueError('incomplete representation')
    data=bytes(values[i] for i in range(total))
    if sha(data)!=expected_hash:raise ValueError('digest mismatch')
    return data

@case(300)
def resumable_bytes():
    # Header strings from RFC 9110 section 14.4; payload below is authored.
    eq(content_range('bytes 42-1233/1234'),(42,1234,1234))
    eq(content_range('bytes 42-1233/*'),(42,1234,None))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:content_range('bytes 4-3/10'))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:content_range('bytes 0-10/10'))
    payload=b'0123456789';etag='"v1"'
    def part(a,b,body,tag=etag,status=206):
        return httpx.Response(status,headers={'etag':tag,
                              'content-range':f'bytes {a}-{b-1}/10'},content=body)
    parts=[part(0,4,payload[:4]),part(4,10,payload[4:])]
    eq(assemble(parts,etag,sha(payload)),payload)
    eq(assemble(list(reversed(parts)),etag,sha(payload)),payload)
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:assemble(parts[:1],etag,sha(payload)))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:assemble([parts[0],part(4,10,payload[4:],'"v2"')],etag,sha(payload)))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:assemble(parts+[part(0,1,b'X')],etag,sha(payload)))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:assemble([part(0,10,payload,status=200)],etag,sha(payload)))
    rejects(ValueError,lambda:assemble(parts,etag,'0'*64))
    fs=fsspec.filesystem('memory')
    path='/proofs-batch11/resumed-evidence'
    fs.pipe_file(path,assemble(parts,etag,sha(payload)))
    eq(fs.cat_file(path),payload)
    return {'verified_bytes':10,'public_range_examples_checked':2,
            'memory_backend_readback':True,'HTTP_range_provider_qualified':False,
            'network_requests':0,'publisher_authenticity_proven_by_hash':False}

def run():
    global ASSERTIONS
    ASSERTIONS=0;results=[]
    for proof,function in CASES:
        before=ASSERTIONS
        try:
            evidence=function();status='passed';error=None
        except Exception:
            evidence={};status='failed';error=traceback.format_exc()
        results.append({'proof':proof,'case':function.__name__,'status':status,
                        'assertions':ASSERTIONS-before,'evidence':evidence,'error':error})
    used=['sympy','networkx','pydantic','rdflib','jsonpointer','httpx','fsspec','Babel']
    return {'scope':'Bounded reference checks only. All ten full chains remain SPECIFIED_NOT_EXECUTED.',
            'source_code_sha256':sha(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
            'python_version':sys.version.split()[0],
            'used_library_versions':{n:importlib.metadata.version(n) for n in used},
            'cases':len(results),'passed':sum(r['status']=='passed' for r in results),
            'failed':sum(r['status']=='failed' for r in results),'assertions':ASSERTIONS,
            'full_chains_executed':0,'public_complete_datasets_ingested':0,
            'live_business_actions':0,'network_requests':0,'results':results}

if __name__=='__main__':
    report=run()
    dest=Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else Path(__file__).with_name('reference-results-291-300.json')
    dest.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2,sort_keys=True,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
    print(json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ['cases','passed','failed','assertions']}))
    for row in report['results']:
        if row['error']:print(row['case'],row['error'])
    raise SystemExit(bool(report['failed']))
```

## Embedded runnable local guard module: handoff_guards_v1.py

SHA256 2b3138b692ecfd02b76ae34bdb001f5046608bb2983d8709d6c55c0765f7c9b8; bytes 19671. Save the following code block as handoff_guards_v1.py.

```python
"""Bounded handoff guards, not replacements for the 300 complete proof chains.
All runtime inputs here are authored fixtures unless explicitly marked as a quote
already present in the user's proof file. No network, LLM, or business actions.
Run: python handoff_guards_v1.py --report report.json
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, copy, hashlib, importlib.metadata, importlib.util, itertools, json, math, re, traceback, unicodedata
from collections import Counter
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal
import networkx as nx
import pandas as pd
import regex
import spacy
from spacy.matcher import PhraseMatcher, Matcher, DependencyMatcher
from spacy.tokens import Doc
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError
from lark import Lark, UnexpectedInput
from jinja2 import Environment, StrictUndefined, UndefinedError
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from dateutil import tz

class Blocked(ValueError):
    """Input is unsuitable for this specified handoff, not evidence of falsity."""

class Port(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, extra='forbid', frozen=True)
    producer: str = Field(min_length=1)
    schema_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
    schema_version: int = Field(ge=1)
    payload_sha256: str = Field(pattern=r'^[0-9a-f]{64}$')
    scope: str = Field(min_length=1)
    basis: Literal['source','mention','candidate','observation','scenario','rendered']
    coverage: Literal['complete','partial','unknown']
    source_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    validation: Literal['passed','failed','not_run','unknown']


def strict_json_loads(raw: str) -> Any:
    def pairs(items):
        out={}
        for k,v in items:
            if k in out: raise Blocked('duplicate JSON member: '+k)
            out[k]=v
        return out
    def bad_constant(x): raise Blocked('nonfinite JSON constant: '+x)
    return json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=pairs, parse_constant=bad_constant)


def canonical_local(value: Any) -> bytes:
    # Local deterministic JSON profile only. This is not RFC 8785/JCS.
    return json.dumps(value,sort_keys=True,ensure_ascii=False,separators=(',',':'),allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8')


def accept_port(port: dict, payload: Any, *, schema: str, scope: str,
                allowed_basis: set[str], require_complete: bool=True) -> Port:
    p=Port.model_validate(port)
    if p.schema_id != schema or p.scope != scope: raise Blocked('schema or scope mismatch')
    if hashlib.sha256(canonical_local(payload)).hexdigest()!=p.payload_sha256: raise Blocked('payload mismatch')
    if p.basis not in allowed_basis: raise Blocked('evidential basis cannot be promoted')
    if not p.source_ids or len(set(p.source_ids))!=len(p.source_ids): raise Blocked('missing or duplicate source IDs')
    if p.validation!='passed': raise Blocked('validation did not pass')
    if require_complete and p.coverage!='complete': raise Blocked('incomplete input population')
    return p


def normalized_span(raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> dict:
    """Map NFC spans only at extended-grapheme-cluster boundaries.
    An internal cluster offset has no unique raw boundary and is rejected.
    """
    pieces=[]; boundaries={0:0}; npos=0
    for m in regex.finditer(r'\X',raw):
        value=unicodedata.normalize('NFC',m.group())
        pieces.append(value); npos+=len(value); boundaries[npos]=m.end()
    normalized=''.join(pieces)
    if normalized!=unicodedata.normalize('NFC',raw): raise Blocked('normalization crosses mapped cluster boundary')
    if type(start) is not int or type(end) is not int or not 0<=start<end<=len(normalized): raise Blocked('invalid span')
    if start not in boundaries or end not in boundaries: raise Blocked('span splits a normalization cluster')
    rs,re_=boundaries[start],boundaries[end]
    result={'normalized_quote':normalized[start:end],'raw_quote':raw[rs:re_],
            'raw_codepoint_span':[rs,re_],'raw_utf8_span':[len(raw[:rs].encode()),len(raw[:re_].encode())]}
    if unicodedata.normalize('NFC',result['raw_quote'])!=result['normalized_quote']:raise Blocked('span check failed')
    return result


def reduce_precedence(g: nx.DiGraph) -> tuple[nx.DiGraph, list[dict]]:
    if type(g) is not nx.DiGraph or not nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(g): raise Blocked('requires a simple DAG')
    for _,_,d in g.edges(data=True):
        if d.get('kind')!='precedence' or not d.get('source_ids'): raise Blocked('untyped or unsupported edge')
    reduced=nx.transitive_reduction(g)
    reduced.graph.update(copy.deepcopy(g.graph))
    reduced.add_nodes_from((n,copy.deepcopy(d)) for n,d in g.nodes(data=True))
    reduced.add_edges_from((u,v,copy.deepcopy(g.edges[u,v])) for u,v in list(reduced.edges))
    removed=[{'from':u,'to':v,'original_attributes':copy.deepcopy(g.edges[u,v]),
              'display_witness':nx.shortest_path(reduced,u,v)} for u,v in g.edges if not reduced.has_edge(u,v)]
    return reduced,removed


def anchored_month(anchor: date | None, months: int) -> date:
    if anchor is None or type(anchor) is not date: raise Blocked('exact date anchor required')
    if type(months) is not int or months<0: raise Blocked('nonnegative whole calendar months required')
    return anchor+relativedelta(months=months)

GRAMMAR=r'''
start: MODAL ACTOR ACTION OBJECT "when" FIELD OP INT
MODAL: "require" | "permit" | "forbid"
ACTOR: /[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*/
ACTION: /[a-z][a-z_]*/
OBJECT: /[a-z][a-z_]*/
FIELD: /[a-z][a-z_]*/
OP: ">=" | ">" | "=="
%import common.INT
%import common.WS
%ignore WS
'''
PARSER=Lark(GRAMMAR,parser='lalr',propagate_positions=True)

def parse_rule(text: str) -> dict:
    try: tree=PARSER.parse(text)
    except UnexpectedInput as e: raise Blocked('unsupported clause; interpretation remains unresolved') from e
    tokens=[str(t) for t in tree.children]
    return dict(zip(['modality','actor','action','object','field','operator','threshold'],tokens)) | {'threshold':int(tokens[-1])}


def validate_process_map(expected: dict[str,str], records: list[dict]) -> dict:
    keys=[r['id'] for r in records]
    if len(keys)!=len(set(keys)): raise Blocked('duplicate BPMN identity')
    if set(keys)!=set(expected): raise Blocked('missing or extra process elements')
    if any(r['kind']!=expected[r['id']] for r in records): raise Blocked('gateway or task semantics changed')
    return {'retained':len(keys)}

class Event(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(strict=True,extra='forbid')
    namespace: str=Field(min_length=1)
    event_id: str=Field(min_length=1)
    case_id: str=Field(min_length=1)
    activity_id: str=Field(min_length=1)
    count: int=Field(ge=0)


def observed_action(kind: str, evidence: dict | None) -> str:
    if kind!='observed_completion' or not evidence: raise Blocked('mention or proposal is not a completed action')
    if not {'case_id','action_id','receipt_id','timestamp'}<=set(evidence): raise Blocked('incomplete occurrence receipt')
    if not all(isinstance(evidence[k],str) and evidence[k] for k in ['case_id','action_id','receipt_id','timestamp']): raise Blocked('empty occurrence field')
    return 'observed'


def disjoint_partition(train: set, test: set, group_by: dict) -> None:
    if not train or not test or train&test: raise Blocked('empty or overlapping partition')
    if not (train|test)<=set(group_by):raise Blocked('missing grouping identity')
    if {group_by[x] for x in train}&{group_by[x] for x in test}: raise Blocked('shared entity leaks across partitions')


def replay_summary(expected_ids: set[str], rows: list[dict], model_role: str) -> dict:
    ids=[r['case_id'] for r in rows]
    if len(ids)!=len(set(ids)) or set(ids)!=expected_ids:raise Blocked('replay population mismatch')
    states=[r['state'] for r in rows]
    allowed={'fit','deviates','not_run','unknown','unsupported'}
    if set(states)-allowed:raise Blocked('unrecognized replay state')
    return {'fit':states.count('fit'),'deviates':states.count('deviates'),
            'unassessed':sum(x in {'not_run','unknown','unsupported'} for x in states),
            'model_role':model_role,'regulatory_compliance_established':False}


def alias_candidates(text: str, lexicon: dict[str,list[str]]) -> list[str]:
    nlp=spacy.blank('en'); matcher=PhraseMatcher(nlp.vocab,attr='LOWER',validate=True)
    for concept,forms in lexicon.items():matcher.add(concept,[nlp.make_doc(f) for f in forms])
    return sorted({nlp.vocab.strings[mid] for mid,_,_ in matcher(nlp.make_doc(text))})


def resolve_alias(text: str, lexicon: dict, *, scope: str, allowed_scope: str,
                  polarity: str, expected_polarity: str) -> str:
    if scope!=allowed_scope or polarity!=expected_polarity:raise Blocked('alias scope or polarity mismatch')
    candidates=alias_candidates(text,lexicon)
    if len(candidates)!=1:raise Blocked('missing or ambiguous approved alias')
    return candidates[0]


def checked_join(left: pd.DataFrame,right: pd.DataFrame,keys:list[str],relation:str='many_to_one') -> pd.DataFrame:
    if not keys:raise Blocked('no identity keys')
    for frame in [left,right]:
        if not set(keys)<=set(frame.columns):raise Blocked('missing join key')
        if frame[keys].isna().any().any():raise Blocked('null identity cannot join')
        if any(not frame[k].map(lambda x:type(x) is str and bool(x)).all() for k in keys):raise Blocked('keys must be exact nonempty string identities')
    result=left.merge(right,on=keys,how='left',validate=relation,indicator=True)
    if not result['_merge'].eq('both').all():raise Blocked('unmatched required rows')
    if len(result)!=len(left):raise Blocked('join changed left row count')
    return result

CASES=[]; ASSERTIONS=0

def require(condition,msg):
    global ASSERTIONS
    ASSERTIONS+=1
    if not condition:raise AssertionError(msg)

def equal(a,b):require(a==b,repr(a)+' != '+repr(b))

def rejects(exc,fn):
    try:fn()
    except exc:require(True,'expected rejection')
    else:require(False,'expected rejection '+exc.__name__)

def case(proof):
    def register(fn):CASES.append((proof,fn));return fn
    return register

@case(1)

    raw='Cafe\u0301 approves.';m=normalized_span(raw,0,4)

    rejects(Blocked,lambda:normalized_span('x',0,2))
    # Authored dependency annotation tests the matcher, not a pretrained parser.
    nlp=spacy.blank('en')
    d=Doc(nlp.vocab,words=['Board','must','not','approve'],heads=[3,3,3,3],deps=['nsubj','aux','neg','ROOT'])
    dm=DependencyMatcher(nlp.vocab)

    equal(len(dm(d)),1)
    return {'normalization_mapping':'checked','unannotated_document_rejected_for_dependency_use':True,'dependency_matcher':'checked on authored parse','statistical_parser_accuracy':'not tested'}
```

```python
"""Second bounded adapter suite. Requires handoff_guards_v1.py from this TXT.
No native Office applications, original chain implementations, or live actions.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, hashlib, json, traceback, copy
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
from datetime import date
import pandas as pd
from pandas.errors import MergeError
import networkx as nx
import handoff_guards_v1 as g


def tally_mentions(rows):
    keys=[(r['source_version'],r['mention_id']) for r in rows]
    if len(keys)!=len(set(keys)):raise g.Blocked('duplicate mention identity')
    if any(r['state'] not in {'approved_tag','ambiguous','unmatched'} for r in rows):raise g.Blocked('unknown mapping state')
    counts=Counter(r['concept_id'] for r in rows if r['state']=='approved_tag')
    if None in counts:raise g.Blocked('missing approved concept')
    return {'mentions':dict(counts),'ambiguous':sum(r['state']=='ambiguous' for r in rows),'unmatched':sum(r['state']=='unmatched' for r in rows),'population':len(rows)}


def case_gaps(rows):
    df=pd.DataFrame(rows)
    required={'case_id','event_id','timestamp'}
    if not required<=set(df):raise g.Blocked('missing event fields')
    if df[['case_id','event_id','timestamp']].isna().any().any():raise g.Blocked('null identity or time')
    if df[['case_id','event_id']].duplicated().any():raise g.Blocked('duplicate event')
    df['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(df['timestamp'],utc=True,errors='raise')
    if df[['case_id','timestamp']].duplicated().any():raise g.Blocked('timestamp ties need causal ordering contract')
    df=df.sort_values(['case_id','timestamp'])
    df['prior']=df.groupby('case_id',dropna=False)['timestamp'].shift(1)
    df['gap']=(df['timestamp']-df['prior']).dt.total_seconds()
    return {r.event_id:None if pd.isna(r.gap) else int(r.gap) for r in df.itertuples()}


def majority_at(meeting:date,rosters:list[dict],present:set[str]):
    rows=[r for r in rosters if r['valid_from']<=meeting<r['valid_to']]
    if len(rows)!=1 or rows[0]['coverage']!='complete':raise g.Blocked('historical voting roster unresolved')
    eligible=rows[0]['voters']
    if not eligible or len(eligible)!=len(set(eligible)):raise g.Blocked('invalid voting population')
    threshold=len(eligible)//2+1
    return {'present_voters':len(present&set(eligible)),'threshold':threshold,'majority_reachable':len(present&set(eligible))>=threshold,'vote_result':None}


def shape_edges(nodes,bindings,edges):
    if set(nodes)!=set(bindings):raise g.Blocked('node binding mismatch')
    if len(set(bindings.values()))!=len(bindings):raise g.Blocked('shape identity reused')
    if any(u not in nodes or v not in nodes for u,v in edges):raise g.Blocked('connector endpoint missing')
    return [(bindings[u],bindings[v]) for u,v in edges]


def typed_readback(before,after):
    # JSON strings encode null/Boolean/number/string distinctions lost by Python
    # equality (True == 1). Row order and repeated values remain significant.
    if g.canonical_local(before)!=g.canonical_local(after):raise g.Blocked('typed ordered content mismatch')
    return True


def dependency_complete(gph,selected):
    if not set(selected)<=set(gph):raise g.Blocked('unknown selected node')
    missing=set().union(*(nx.ancestors(gph,n) for n in selected))-set(selected) if selected else set()
    if missing:raise g.Blocked('missing prerequisites: '+','.join(sorted(missing)))
    return True
```

## Checkpoint integrity and environment for this batch

Head revision: the current TXT carries six lines after the P20 checkpoint that are not part of any checkpoint, lines 9-14 of the head (the core rule and the custom-glue paragraph). The P20 checkpoint hash 644e56e9ecce1fba644e9f1bdb7771d931e130bd530bdc440e75eac36bdd1ef7 reproduces from the current bytes only with those six lines removed, and the frozen master hash 78b168344b86014d4cbd5475b12e9c462aab0142d95f895c166ab1b7155bd932 (919254 bytes) reproduces as lines 1-14264 without them. The current head, with the six lines, is the base of this batch: its SHA256 is the prior cumulative TXT SHA256 recorded at the end of this batch. All twenty recorded section hashes for P1-P20 and both embedded modules and evidence files reproduce byte for byte from the current TXT.

Core rule applied from this batch on: every comparison, join, interval test, difference, similarity, grounding, and execution in the guard code is a library primitive call; local code declares fixtures and policies and turns primitive results into Blocked outcomes. Local control flow that re-implements such an operation where a primitive exists is a defect. Earlier modules stay unchanged under HG07; their substitutes live in handoff_guards_v3.py with agreement tests (see the glue register below).

Environment: Python 3.11.15 in an isolated virtual environment; the package index was reachable through the environment's egress proxy, so every library named below was installed and executed at the version recorded in guards-v3.json. pandas is pinned to 2.2.3, the version recorded in the augmentation pins and in guards-v1/v2; pandas 3.0.5 was also exercised and raises ValueError where 2.2.3 warns (P21). The WordNet 3.0 corpus (corpora/wordnet.zip, 10775600 bytes, SHA256 cbda5ea6eef7f36a97a43d4a75f85e07fccbb4f23657d27b4ccbc93e2646ab59) was fetched once before the run with NLTK's proxied-download opt-in; the guard run itself made no network call. Documentation hosts duckdb.org, pandas.pydata.org, zepworks.com, readthedocs.io, scikit-learn.org, plotly.com, networkx.org, potassco.org, processintelligence.solutions and omg.org are blocked by the egress policy, so function references were checked on GitHub-hosted sources at the pinned version where available and against the installed docstrings; each reference states which.

Reproduction of the earlier checkpoints: handoff_guards_v1.py (SHA256 2b3138b692ecfd02b76ae34bdb001f5046608bb2983d8709d6c55c0765f7c9b8) and handoff_guards_v2.py (SHA256 0a406d0e5f6b8b1b931d6786ed1d8e95fef39b79106eae8852703f9394952538), extracted from this TXT, pass 10 of 10 cases each (70 and 34 assertions) in this environment. [HD48] openpyxl types a cell whose string value starts with '=' as a formula at write time (Cell.data_type 'f'); load_workbook(data_only=False) returns the formula text and data_only=True the cached value, None when nothing computed it (HD22). Executed with 3.1.5.
